Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards

An engineering manual analyzing recursive decision trees, prefix-suffix splits, sliding window complement optimization, and circular pointer pivoting.

Problem Statement

There are several cards arranged in a row, and each card has an associated number of points. The points are given in the integer array cardPoints.

In one step, you can take one card from the beginning or from the end of the row. You must take exactly k cards.

Your score is the sum of the points of the cards you have taken. Return the maximum score you can obtain.

Constraints

  • 1 <= cardPoints.length <= 10^5
  • 1 <= cardPoints[i] <= 10^4
  • 1 <= k <= cardPoints.length

Visualizing the Intent

Let's map out how picking cards from the edges bounds the choices:

Input: cardPoints = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1], k = 3 Options for picking k = 3 cards from ends: - Take 3 from left, 0 from right : [1, 2, 3] -> Sum = 6 - Take 2 from left, 1 from right : [1, 2] + [1] -> Sum = 4 - Take 1 from left, 2 from right : [1] + [6, 1] -> Sum = 8 - Take 0 from left, 3 from right : [] + [5, 6, 1] -> Sum = 12 Maximum Obtainable Score = 12

Core Realization: Since we can only pick cards from the start or the end of the array, any valid selection of k cards consists of i cards taken from the left prefix and k - i cards taken from the right suffix (where 0 <= i <= k).

Solutions Breakdown

Approach 1 - Brute Force (Recursive Decision Tree)

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (Branching Choices)

1. The Concept: At each step, we have two choices: pick the card at the current left pointer or pick the card at the current right pointer. We can write a recursive function solve(left, right, k) that explores both paths and returns the maximum sum possible.

2. Why it Fails Constraints: At every step, the function branches into 2 choices. For k decisions, the decision tree grows exponentially with O(2^k) branches. When k can be as large as 10^5, this recursive solution will hit a Stack Overflow or Time Limit Exceeded (TLE) error almost immediately.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition: Har step par humare paas 2 options hain: ya toh leftmost card uthao ya rightmost card. Recursion se dono options try karke max return kar do. Iska Time Complexity O(2^k) hota hai kyuki har choice par 2 naye paths bante hain. Jab k bada hoga, code TLE de dega.

📋 Approach 1 Trace Profile

Input: cardPoints = [1, 2, 3], k = 2

Recursion Tree: solve(left=0, right=2, k=2) / \ Pick Left (1) Pick Right (3) solve(left=1, right=2, k=1) solve(left=0, right=1, k=1) / \ / \ Pick Left (2) Pick Right (3) Pick Left (1) Pick Right (2) 1 + 2 = 3 1 + 3 = 4 3 + 1 = 4 3 + 2 = 5 Max Score = max(3, 4, 4, 5) = 5

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, cardPoints: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        # Recursive helper function exploring left and right choices
        def solve(left: int, right: int, cards_left: int) -> int:
            if cards_left == 0:
                return 0  # Base case: no more cards to pick

            # Choice 1: Take card from the left end
            pick_left = cardPoints[left] + solve(left + 1, right, cards_left - 1)
            # Choice 2: Take card from the right end
            pick_right = cardPoints[right] + solve(left, right - 1, cards_left - 1)

            return max(pick_left, pick_right)

        return solve(0, len(cardPoints) - 1, k)
class Solution {
private:
    int solve(const vector<int>& cardPoints, int left, int right, int k) {
        if (k == 0) return 0;

        int pickLeft = cardPoints[left] + solve(cardPoints, left + 1, right, k - 1);
        int pickRight = cardPoints[right] + solve(cardPoints, left, right - 1, k - 1);

        return max(pickLeft, pickRight);
    }

public:
    int maxScore(vector<int>& cardPoints, int k) {
        return solve(cardPoints, 0, cardPoints.size() - 1, k);
    }
};
class Solution {
    private int solve(int[] cardPoints, int left, int right, int k) {
        if (k == 0) return 0;

        int pickLeft = cardPoints[left] + solve(cardPoints, left + 1, right, k - 1);
        int pickRight = cardPoints[right] + solve(cardPoints, left, right - 1, k - 1);

        return Math.max(pickLeft, pickRight);
    }

    public int maxScore(int[] cardPoints, int k) {
        return solve(cardPoints, 0, cardPoints.length - 1, k);
    }
}
var maxScore = function(cardPoints, k) {
    const solve = (left, right, cardsLeft) => {
        if (cardsLeft === 0) return 0;

        let pickLeft = cardPoints[left] + solve(left + 1, right, cardsLeft - 1);
        let pickRight = cardPoints[right] + solve(left, right - 1, cardsLeft - 1);

        return Math.max(pickLeft, pickRight);
    };

    return solve(0, cardPoints.length - 1, k);
};

Approach 2 - Better Solution: Prefix & Suffix Sum Arrays

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (Precomputing Edge Sums)

1. Structural Realization: Any valid pick of k cards consists of taking i cards from the front and k - i cards from the back, where i ranges from 0 to k.

There are only k + 1 possible split configurations!

Split Configurations for k = 3: - Config 0: 3 from left, 0 from right -> prefix[3] + suffix[0] - Config 1: 2 from left, 1 from right -> prefix[2] + suffix[1] - Config 2: 1 from left, 2 from right -> prefix[1] + suffix[2] - Config 3: 0 from left, 3 from right -> prefix[0] + suffix[3]

2. How it Works:
• Build a prefix_sum array of size k + 1 where prefix_sum[i] stores the sum of the first i cards from the left.
• Build a suffix_sum array of size k + 1 where suffix_sum[i] stores the sum of the last i cards from the right.
• Loop i from 0 to k, calculating current_score = prefix_sum[i] + suffix_sum[k - i].
• Take the maximum across all k + 1 configurations.

This optimizes time complexity down to O(K)! However, allocating auxiliary prefix and suffix arrays uses O(K) extra space.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition: Notice karo ki k cards pick karne ke kul k + 1 combinations hote hain. Ya toh i cards left se uthao aur k - i cards right se.

Hum do arrays banate hain: prefix_sum (shuruat ke k cards ka cumulative sum) aur suffix_sum (aakhri k cards ka cumulative sum). Phir ek loop chala kar prefix_sum[i] + suffix_sum[k - i] check kar lete hain. Isse time complexity O(K) ho jati hai, lekin extra space O(K) lagti hai.

📋 Approach 2 Trace Dry Run

Input: cardPoints = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1], k = 3

Build Prefix Sums (first 3 cards from left): • prefix[0] = 0 • prefix[1] = 1 • prefix[2] = 1 + 2 = 3 • prefix[3] = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 prefix = [0, 1, 3, 6] Build Suffix Sums (last 3 cards from right): • suffix[0] = 0 • suffix[1] = 1 • suffix[2] = 1 + 6 = 7 • suffix[3] = 1 + 6 + 5 = 12 suffix = [0, 1, 7, 12] Evaluate all i from 0 to k=3: • i = 0: score = prefix[0] + suffix[3] = 0 + 12 = 12 • i = 1: score = prefix[1] + suffix[2] = 1 + 7 = 8 • i = 2: score = prefix[2] + suffix[1] = 3 + 1 = 4 • i = 3: score = prefix[3] + suffix[0] = 6 + 0 = 6 Max Score = max(12, 8, 4, 6) = 12

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, cardPoints: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(cardPoints)
        prefix = [0] * (k + 1)
        suffix = [0] * (k + 1)

        # Precompute prefix sum for first k cards
        for i in range(1, k + 1):
            prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + cardPoints[i - 1]

        # Precompute suffix sum for last k cards
        for i in range(1, k + 1):
            suffix[i] = suffix[i - 1] + cardPoints[n - i]

        max_points = 0
        # Compare all combinations of picking i cards from left and k - i from right
        for i in range(k + 1):
            current_score = prefix[i] + suffix[k - i]
            max_points = max(max_points, current_score)

        return max_points
class Solution {
public:
    int maxScore(vector<int>& cardPoints, int k) {
        int n = cardPoints.size();
        vector<int> prefix(k + 1, 0);
        vector<int> suffix(k + 1, 0);

        for (int i = 1; i <= k; ++i) {
            prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + cardPoints[i - 1];
        }

        for (int i = 1; i <= k; ++i) {
            suffix[i] = suffix[i - 1] + cardPoints[n - i];
        }

        int maxPoints = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i <= k; ++i) {
            int currentScore = prefix[i] + suffix[k - i];
            maxPoints = max(maxPoints, currentScore);
        }

        return maxPoints;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int maxScore(int[] cardPoints, int k) {
        int n = cardPoints.length;
        int[] prefix = new int[k + 1];
        int[] suffix = new int[k + 1];

        for (int i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
            prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + cardPoints[i - 1];
        }

        for (int i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
            suffix[i] = suffix[i - 1] + cardPoints[n - i];
        }

        int maxPoints = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i <= k; i++) {
            int currentScore = prefix[i] + suffix[k - i];
            maxPoints = Math.max(maxPoints, currentScore);
        }

        return maxPoints;
    }
}
var maxScore = function(cardPoints, k) {
    const n = cardPoints.length;
    const prefix = new Array(k + 1).fill(0);
    const suffix = new Array(k + 1).fill(0);

    for (let i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
        prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + cardPoints[i - 1];
    }

    for (let i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
        suffix[i] = suffix[i - 1] + cardPoints[n - i];
    }

    let maxPoints = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= k; i++) {
        let currentScore = prefix[i] + suffix[k - i];
        maxPoints = Math.max(maxPoints, currentScore);
    }

    return maxPoints;
};

Approach 3 - Optimal Solution: Constant Space Circular Pointer Shift (Sliding Window)

🧭 Deep Intuition Breakdown (In-Place Pivot Shift)

1. The Architectural Discovery: Instead of allocating extra memory arrays for prefix and suffix sums, we can simulate the split transition dynamically in-place using two scalar sum variables!

2. How the Shift Engine Operates:
• Initial Baseline State: Assume we pick ALL k cards from the left end! Compute left_sum = sum(cardPoints[0...k-1]) and set right_sum = 0. Set initial max_score = left_sum.
• Step-by-Step Transition: We dynamically transfer cards from the left pick set to the right pick set one by one!

In each of the k steps: 1. Remove 1 card from the left sum: left_sum -= cardPoints[left_ptr] 2. Add 1 card to the right sum: right_sum += cardPoints[right_ptr] 3. Update max_score: max_score = max(max_score, left_sum + right_sum) 4. Decrement left_ptr, Decrement right_ptr

3. Why Space is O(1) and Time is O(K):
We only need two integer pointers (left_ptr and right_ptr) and running sum accumulators. This reduces memory usage to O(1) auxiliary space while performing exactly k constant-time updates (O(K) time)!

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition behind Optimal Pointer Shift: Extra memory arrays (prefix/suffix) banane ki bilkul zaroorat nahi hai.

• Initial State: Shuruat me maan lo humne saare k cards **LEFT side** se utha liye. Uska sum left_sum me save kar lo. Baseline score: max_score = left_sum.
• Shift Operations: Ab ek-ek karke left side se 1 card kam karte jao (left_sum -= cardPoints[left_ptr]) aur right side se 1 card badhate jao (right_sum += cardPoints[right_ptr]).
• Har step par max_score ko update karo. Isse bina kisi extra space ke (O(1) Memory) aur sirf O(K) Time me optimal answer mil jata hai!

📋 Full Line-by-Line Trace Dry Run 1: Standard Input

Input: cardPoints = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1], k = 3 (N = 7)

================================================================================= INITIALIZATION: ================================================================================= • Pick all k = 3 cards from left: left_sum = cardPoints[0] + cardPoints[1] + cardPoints[2] = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 right_sum = 0 max_score = 6 • Pointer Setup: left_ptr = k - 1 = 2 (points to value 3) right_ptr = n - 1 = 6 (points to value 1) ================================================================================= STEP 1: Drop 1 card from left (index 2), pick 1 card from right (index 6) ================================================================================= • left_sum -= cardPoints[2] (3) -> left_sum = 6 - 3 = 3 • right_sum += cardPoints[6] (1) -> right_sum = 0 + 1 = 1 • current_score = 3 + 1 = 4 • max_score = max(6, 4) = 6 • Update Pointers: left_ptr = 1, right_ptr = 5 ================================================================================= STEP 2: Drop 1 card from left (index 1), pick 1 card from right (index 5) ================================================================================= • left_sum -= cardPoints[1] (2) -> left_sum = 3 - 2 = 1 • right_sum += cardPoints[5] (6) -> right_sum = 1 + 6 = 7 • current_score = 1 + 7 = 8 • max_score = max(6, 8) = 8 • Update Pointers: left_ptr = 0, right_ptr = 4 ================================================================================= STEP 3: Drop 1 card from left (index 0), pick 1 card from right (index 4) ================================================================================= • left_sum -= cardPoints[0] (1) -> left_sum = 1 - 1 = 0 • right_sum += cardPoints[4] (5) -> right_sum = 7 + 5 = 12 • current_score = 0 + 12 = 12 • max_score = max(8, 12) = 12 • Update Pointers: left_ptr = -1, right_ptr = 3 ================================================================================= TERMINATION: ================================================================================= • left_ptr < 0. Loop terminates cleanly! • Return max_score -> 12. Final Answer Returned: 12
📋 Full Line-by-Line Trace Dry Run 2: Corner Pick Optimization

Input: cardPoints = [2, 2, 2], k = 2 (N = 3)

Initialization: • left_sum = 2 + 2 = 4, right_sum = 0, max_score = 4 • left_ptr = 1, right_ptr = 2 • Shift 1: - left_sum -= cardPoints[1] (2) -> left_sum = 2 - right_sum += cardPoints[2] (2) -> right_sum = 2 - current_score = 2 + 2 = 4 -> max_score = 4 - left_ptr = 0, right_ptr = 1 • Shift 2: - left_sum -= cardPoints[0] (2) -> left_sum = 0 - right_sum += cardPoints[1] (2) -> right_sum = 4 - current_score = 0 + 4 = 4 -> max_score = 4 - left_ptr = -1, right_ptr = 0 Loop terminates. Returns 4

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, cardPoints: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(cardPoints)
        
        # Step 1: Initial state - pick all k cards from left side
        left_sum = sum(cardPoints[:k])
        right_sum = 0
        max_score = left_sum

        left_ptr = k - 1  # Points to last picked card on left
        right_ptr = n - 1  # Points to rightmost unpicked card

        # Step 2: Gradually shift cards from left pick set to right pick set
        while left_ptr >= 0:
            left_sum -= cardPoints[left_ptr]  # Remove card from left sum
            right_sum += cardPoints[right_ptr]  # Add card to right sum
            max_score = max(max_score, left_sum + right_sum)  # Track maximum total
            
            left_ptr -= 1  # Move left pointer backward
            right_ptr -= 1  # Move right pointer backward

        return max_score  # Return maximum score obtained
class Solution {
public:
    int maxScore(vector<int>& cardPoints, int k) {
        int n = cardPoints.size();
        int leftSum = 0, rightSum = 0;

        // Calculate initial sum of all k cards from the left
        for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) {
            leftSum += cardPoints[i];
        }

        int maxScore = leftSum;
        int leftPtr = k - 1;
        int rightPtr = n - 1;

        // Shift pivot from left to right dynamically
        while (leftPtr >= 0) {
            leftSum -= cardPoints[leftPtr];
            rightSum += cardPoints[rightPtr];
            maxScore = max(maxScore, leftSum + rightSum);
            leftPtr--;
            rightPtr--;
        }

        return maxScore;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int maxScore(int[] cardPoints, int k) {
        int n = cardPoints.length;
        int leftSum = 0, rightSum = 0;

        // Seed leftSum with first k cards
        for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
            leftSum += cardPoints[i];
        }

        int maxScore = leftSum;
        int leftPtr = k - 1;
        int rightPtr = n - 1;

        // Shift cards from left to right
        while (leftPtr >= 0) {
            leftSum -= cardPoints[leftPtr];
            rightSum += cardPoints[rightPtr];
            maxScore = Math.max(maxScore, leftSum + rightSum);
            leftPtr--;
            rightPtr--;
        }

        return maxScore;
    }
}
var maxScore = function(cardPoints, k) {
    const n = cardPoints.length;
    let leftSum = 0, rightSum = 0;

    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
        leftSum += cardPoints[i];
    }

    let maxScore = leftSum;
    let leftPtr = k - 1;
    let rightPtr = n - 1;

    while (leftPtr >= 0) {
        leftSum -= cardPoints[leftPtr];
        rightSum += cardPoints[rightPtr];
        maxScore = Math.max(maxScore, leftSum + rightSum);
        leftPtr--;
        rightPtr--;
    }

    return maxScore;
};

Strategic Edge Cases Tracking Matrix

Edge Case Profile Algorithmic Risk Factor Mitigation Resolution Logic
k == n (Pick All Cards)
e.g., cardPoints = [2, 2, 2], k = 3		 Index out of bounds or negative array accessing when shifting pointers. Initial leftSum includes all n elements. When k == n, shifting loop executes, but total sum remains equal across all iterations. Handled safely.
k == 1 (Pick Single Card)
e.g., cardPoints = [9, 100, 1], k = 1		 Failing to evaluate single left vs single right comparison. Initial leftSum = cardPoints[0] = 9. Loop shifts 1 step: leftSum = 0, rightSum = 1. Evaluates max(9, 1) = 9. Correct!
All Cards Identical Values
e.g., cardPoints = [5, 5, 5, 5, 5], k = 2		 Sub-optimal pointer evaluations. Score sum evaluates to 5 * k = 10 across all split points. maxScore returns 10 cleanly.

Complexity Analysis Performance Metrics

Approach Category Time Complexity Space Complexity Performance Evaluation Rating
Approach 1: Brute Force Recursion O(2^K) O(K) Stack Fails Constraints (TLE). Exponential decision tree branching. Fails for K > 30.
Approach 2: Prefix & Suffix Sum Arrays O(K) O(K) Space Linear Time / Sub-Optimal Memory. Allocates auxiliary arrays for prefix and suffix sums.
Approach 3: Constant Space Pointer Shift O(K) O(1) Auxiliary Absolute Production Standard. Executes exactly K pivot iterations in O(K) time using zero extra memory arrays. Maximum efficiency.

Maximum Population Year

An engineering manual analyzing direct counting, event sweep-line sorting, and optimal prefix-sum line sweep algorithms.

Problem Statement

You are given a 2D integer array logs where each logs[i] = [birth_i, death_i] indicates the birth and death years of the i-th person.

The population of some year x is the number of people alive during that year. The i-th person is counted in year x's population if x is in the inclusive range [birth_i, death_i - 1]. Note that the person is not counted in the year that they die.

Return the earliest year with the maximum population.

Constraints

  • 1 <= logs.length <= 100
  • 1950 <= birth_i < death_i <= 2050

Visualizing the Intent

Let's map out how lifespans overlap across specific years:

Input: logs = [[1993, 1999], [2000, 2010]] Person 1: Alive in years [1993, 1994, 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998] (Dies in 1999) Person 2: Alive in years [2000, 2001, ..., 2009] (Dies in 2010) Year Population Map: 1993 - 1998: Population = 1 1999 : Population = 0 (Person 1 died, Person 2 not born) 2000 - 2009: Population = 1 Maximum Population = 1 Earliest Year with Population 1 = 1993 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Input: logs = [[1950, 1961], [1960, 1971], [1970, 1981]] Years alive per person: P1: 1950 - 1960 P2: 1960 - 1970 P3: 1970 - 1980 Checking year 1960: - P1 is alive in 1960 (death is 1961). - P2 is alive in 1960 (birth is 1960). - Population at 1960 = 2! Earliest Maximum Population Year = 1960

Core Realization: A birth at year Y increases the population by +1 for year Y onward. A death at year Y decreases the population by -1 starting at year Y. We need to aggregate these net delta changes across the timeline.

Solutions Breakdown

Approach 1 - Brute Force (Direct Year Population Hash Map)

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (Year-by-Year Frequency Array)

1. The Concept: Iterate through every person's log [birth, death]. For each year year in the range birth to death - 1, increment a frequency counter array or Hash Map for that year.

2. Finding the Answer: After updating all years for all persons, iterate through the years from 1950 to 2050 and pick the earliest year that recorded the maximum population.

3. Complexity: For N people and a lifespan range of Y years (up to 100 years), time complexity is O(N * Y). Given constraints (N <= 100, Y <= 100), total operations are around 10,000, which easily passes, but is inefficient compared to linear methods.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition: Har insaan ke log ko uthao, aur uske birth se lekar death - 1 tak ke saare saalon (years) ki population ko +1 se badha do (ek simple array ya hash map me). Phir 1950 se 2050 tak scan karke dekho ki kis saal sabse jyada population thi. Isme O(N * Y) time lagta hai.

📋 Approach 1 Line-by-Line Trace Profile

Input: logs = [[1950, 1953], [1951, 1953]]

Initialize population array pop_map of size 101 for years [1950...2050] • Log 0: [1950, 1953] -> Alive in [1950, 1951, 1952] - pop_map[1950] += 1 (val = 1) - pop_map[1951] += 1 (val = 1) - pop_map[1952] += 1 (val = 1) • Log 1: [1951, 1953] -> Alive in [1951, 1952] - pop_map[1951] += 1 (val = 2) - pop_map[1952] += 1 (val = 2) Scan pop_map from 1950 to 2050: - 1950: pop = 1 - 1951: pop = 2 -> Max pop = 2, year = 1951 - 1952: pop = 2 -> Max pop = 2, earliest year remains 1951 Return 1951

a) Source Code Implementation

class BruteForceSolution:
    def maximumPopulation(self, logs: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        pop_map = [0] * 101  # Index 0 corresponds to year 1950

        for birth, death in logs:
            # Increment population for each year person was alive
            for year in range(birth, death):
                pop_map[year - 1950] += 1

        max_pop = 0
        earliest_year = 1950

        # Find year with maximum population
        for i in range(101):
            if pop_map[i] > max_pop:
                max_pop = pop_map[i]
                earliest_year = 1950 + i

        return earliest_year
class BruteForceSolution {
public:
    int maximumPopulation(vector<vector<int>>& logs) {
        vector<int> popMap(101, 0);

        for (const auto& log : logs) {
            int birth = log[0];
            int death = log[1];
            for (int year = birth; year < death; ++year) {
                popMap[year - 1950]++;
            }
        }

        int maxPop = 0;
        int earliestYear = 1950;

        for (int i = 0; i < 101; ++i) {
            if (popMap[i] > maxPop) {
                maxPop = popMap[i];
                earliestYear = 1950 + i;
            }
        }

        return earliestYear;
    }
};
class BruteForceSolution {
    public int maximumPopulation(int[][] logs) {
        int[] popMap = new int[101];

        for (int[] log : logs) {
            int birth = log[0];
            int death = log[1];
            for (int year = birth; year < death; year++) {
                popMap[year - 1950]++;
            }
        }

        int maxPop = 0;
        int earliestYear = 1950;

        for (int i = 0; i < 101; i++) {
            if (popMap[i] > maxPop) {
                maxPop = popMap[i];
                earliestYear = 1950 + i;
            }
        }

        return earliestYear;
    }
}
var maximumPopulation = function(logs) {
    const popMap = new Array(101).fill(0);

    for (let [birth, death] of logs) {
        for (let year = birth; year < death; year++) {
            popMap[year - 1950]++;
        }
    }

    let maxPop = 0;
    let earliestYear = 1950;

    for (let i = 0; i < 101; i++) {
        if (popMap[i] > maxPop) {
            maxPop = popMap[i];
            earliestYear = 1950 + i;
        }
    }

    return earliestYear;
};

Approach 2 - Event-Based Sweep Line (Sorting Events)

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (Event Timeline Stream)

1. The Concept: Break down each person's lifespan into two discrete timestamp events:

  • A Birth Event: (birth_year, +1)
  • A Death Event: (death_year, -1)

2. Sorting Rules: Place all 2 * N events into an array and sort them chronologically by year.
If a birth and death occur in the exact same year, process the death event (-1) before or ensure that death at year Y does not count toward year Y's population. Sorting naturally arranges events along a continuous timeline.

3. Running Sum Execution: Iterate through the sorted events, adding the delta value (+1 or -1) to a running population total. Track the peak running sum and record the year it was achieved.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition: Lifespan ko 2 events me tod do: (birth_year, +1) aur (death_year, -1). Saare events ko ek list me daal kar saal (year) ke hisab se sort kar do. Phir chronology me ek-ek event process karte hue running population maintain karo. Isme O(N log N) time lagta hai sorting ki wajah se.

📋 Approach 2 Trace Profile

Input: logs = [[1950, 1961], [1960, 1971]]

Events Generated: • (1950, +1) • (1961, -1) • (1960, +1) • (1971, -1) Sorted Events: 1. Year 1950: delta = +1 2. Year 1960: delta = +1 3. Year 1961: delta = -1 4. Year 1971: delta = -1 Process Timeline: • Year 1950: running_pop = 0 + 1 = 1 -> max_pop = 1, year = 1950 • Year 1960: running_pop = 1 + 1 = 2 -> max_pop = 2, year = 1960 • Year 1961: running_pop = 2 - 1 = 1 • Year 1971: running_pop = 1 - 1 = 0 Result = 1960

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def maximumPopulation(self, logs: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        events = []
        for birth, death in logs:
            events.append((birth, 1))   # Birth increases population
            events.append((death, -1))   # Death decreases population

        # Sort events chronologically. If years tie, -1 (death) comes before +1 (birth)
        events.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))

        max_pop = 0
        running_pop = 0
        earliest_year = 1950

        for year, change in events:
            running_pop += change
            if running_pop > max_pop:
                max_pop = running_pop
                earliest_year = year

        return earliest_year
class Solution {
public:
    int maximumPopulation(vector<vector<int>>& logs) {
        vector<pair<int, int>> events;
        for (const auto& log : logs) {
            events.push_back({log[0], 1});
            events.push_back({log[1], -1});
        }

        // Sort events
        sort(events.begin(), events.end());

        int maxPop = 0, runningPop = 0, earliestYear = 1950;
        for (const auto& event : events) {
            runningPop += event.second;
            if (runningPop > maxPop) {
                maxPop = runningPop;
                earliestYear = event.first;
            }
        }

        return earliestYear;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int maximumPopulation(int[][] logs) {
        List<int[]> events = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int[] log : logs) {
            events.add(new int[]{log[0], 1});
            events.add(new int[]{log[1], -1});
        }

        // Sort events by year, breaking ties by change
        events.sort((a, b) -> a[0] == b[0] ? Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]) : Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));

        int maxPop = 0, runningPop = 0, earliestYear = 1950;
        for (int[] event : events) {
            runningPop += event[1];
            if (runningPop > maxPop) {
                maxPop = runningPop;
                earliestYear = event[0];
            }
        }

        return earliestYear;
    }
}
var maximumPopulation = function(logs) {
    const events = [];
    for (let [birth, death] of logs) {
        events.push([birth, 1]);
        events.push([death, -1]);
    }

    events.sort((a, b) => a[0] === b[0] ? a[1] - b[1] : a[0] - b[0]);

    let maxPop = 0, runningPop = 0, earliestYear = 1950;
    for (let [year, change] of events) {
        runningPop += change;
        if (runningPop > maxPop) {
            maxPop = runningPop;
            earliestYear = year;
        }
    }

    return earliestYear;
};

Approach 3 - Optimal Solution: Line Sweep Difference Array (Prefix Sum)

🧭 Deep Intuition Breakdown (Difference Array & Prefix Sum)

1. Fixed Bounded Range: The problem guarantees that all years lie strictly between 1950 and 2050. This fixed range spans exactly 101 years!

2. The Difference Array Optimization:
Instead of sorting events, we can map years directly to an array year_delta of size 101 (where index 0 represents 1950 and index 100 represents 2050).

For each log [birth, death]: 1. year_delta[birth - 1950] += 1 (Population increases at birth year) 2. year_delta[death - 1950] -= 1 (Population decreases at death year)

3. Running Prefix Sum Accumulation:
Once all logs are marked in O(N) time, a single linear scan from index 0 to 100 maintains a running prefix sum of year_delta. The running sum directly gives the exact population for each year in chronological order!

4. Time & Space Guarantee:
• Time: O(N) to process logs + O(101) to calculate prefix sums = O(N).
• Space: O(101) = O(1) auxiliary space!

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition behind Line Sweep: Humaari range fixed hai (1950-2050 -> total 101 saal). Hum ek size 101 ka difference array year_delta banate hain.

• Birth year par: year_delta[birth - 1950] += 1 karo.
• Death year par: year_delta[death - 1950] -= 1 karo.
• Phir array par ek single pass chala kar **Prefix Sum** nikalo. Prefix sum hume har saal ki exact population de dega. Maximum population record karke sabse pehla (earliest) saal return kar do. Space O(1) hai aur Time O(N) hai!

📋 Full Line-by-Line Trace Dry Run 1: Overlapping Lifespans

Input: logs = [[1950, 1961], [1960, 1971], [1970, 1981]]

================================================================================= STEP 1: MARK DIFFERENCE ARRAY (year_delta of size 101) ================================================================================= • Log 0: [1950, 1961] - year_delta[1950 - 1950] += 1 -> year_delta[0] = +1 - year_delta[1961 - 1950] -= 1 -> year_delta[11] = -1 • Log 1: [1960, 1971] - year_delta[1960 - 1950] += 1 -> year_delta[10] = +1 - year_delta[1971 - 1950] -= 1 -> year_delta[21] = -1 • Log 2: [1970, 1981] - year_delta[1970 - 1950] += 1 -> year_delta[20] = +1 - year_delta[1981 - 1950] -= 1 -> year_delta[31] = -1 ================================================================================= STEP 2: PREFIX SUM SCAN (index 0 to 100) ================================================================================= • i = 0 (Year 1950): running_pop += year_delta[0] (+1) -> pop = 1 - max_pop = 1, earliest_year = 1950 • i = 1 to 9 (Years 1951 - 1959): year_delta = 0 -> pop remains 1 • i = 10 (Year 1960): running_pop += year_delta[10] (+1) -> pop = 1 + 1 = 2 - pop (2) > max_pop (1) -> max_pop = 2, earliest_year = 1960 • i = 11 (Year 1961): running_pop += year_delta[11] (-1) -> pop = 2 - 1 = 1 • i = 12 to 19 (Years 1962 - 1969): pop remains 1 • i = 20 (Year 1970): running_pop += year_delta[20] (+1) -> pop = 1 + 1 = 2 - pop (2) is NOT strictly greater than max_pop (2) -> earliest_year stays 1960! • i = 21 (Year 1971): running_pop += year_delta[21] (-1) -> pop = 2 - 1 = 1 FINAL RETURNED YEAR: 1960
📋 Full Line-by-Line Trace Dry Run 2: Same Year Birth/Death Alignment

Input: logs = [[2000, 2005], [2005, 2010]]

Marking Delta Array: • Log 0: [2000, 2005] -> delta[2000] += 1, delta[2005] -= 1 • Log 1: [2005, 2010] -> delta[2005] += 1, delta[2010] -= 1 Notice at index 2005: delta[2005] = (-1) + (+1) = 0! Prefix Sum Scan: • Year 2000: running_pop = 1 -> max_pop = 1, year = 2000 • Year 2001 - 2004: running_pop = 1 • Year 2005: running_pop += delta[2005] (0) -> running_pop = 1 (Person 1 died, Person 2 born. Net population change = 0. Correct!) Returns 2000

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def maximumPopulation(self, logs: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        # Fixed range array covering years 1950 through 2050
        year_delta = [0] * 101

        # Mark birth and death deltas in O(N)
        for birth, death in logs:
            year_delta[birth - 1950] += 1
            year_delta[death - 1950] -= 1

        max_pop = 0
        running_pop = 0
        earliest_year = 1950

        # Compute prefix sum to find peak population year
        for i in range(101):
            running_pop += year_delta[i]
            if running_pop > max_pop:
                max_pop = running_pop
                earliest_year = 1950 + i

        return earliest_year
class Solution {
public:
    int maximumPopulation(vector<vector<int>>& logs) {
        vector<int> yearDelta(101, 0);

        // Mark changes
        for (const auto& log : logs) {
            yearDelta[log[0] - 1950]++;
            yearDelta[log[1] - 1950]--;
        }

        int maxPop = 0;
        int runningPop = 0;
        int earliestYear = 1950;

        // Prefix sum scan
        for (int i = 0; i < 101; ++i) {
            runningPop += yearDelta[i];
            if (runningPop > maxPop) {
                maxPop = runningPop;
                earliestYear = 1950 + i;
            }
        }

        return earliestYear;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int maximumPopulation(int[][] logs) {
        int[] yearDelta = new int[101];

        // Record birth/death deltas
        for (int[] log : logs) {
            yearDelta[log[0] - 1950]++;
            yearDelta[log[1] - 1950]--;
        }

        int maxPop = 0;
        int runningPop = 0;
        int earliestYear = 1950;

        // Compute prefix sum
        for (int i = 0; i < 101; i++) {
            runningPop += yearDelta[i];
            if (runningPop > maxPop) {
                maxPop = runningPop;
                earliestYear = 1950 + i;
            }
        }

        return earliestYear;
    }
}
var maximumPopulation = function(logs) {
    const yearDelta = new Array(101).fill(0);

    // Record deltas
    for (let [birth, death] of logs) {
        yearDelta[birth - 1950]++;
        yearDelta[death - 1950]--;
    }

    let maxPop = 0;
    let runningPop = 0;
    let earliestYear = 1950;

    // Sweep line prefix sum
    for (let i = 0; i < 101; i++) {
        runningPop += yearDelta[i];
        if (runningPop > maxPop) {
            maxPop = runningPop;
            earliestYear = 1950 + i;
        }
    }

    return earliestYear;
};

Strategic Edge Cases Tracking Matrix

Edge Case Profile Algorithmic Risk Factor Mitigation Resolution Logic
Birth and Death in Consecutively Adjacent Years
e.g., [1950, 1951]		 Counting person in year of death. In difference array, delta[0] = +1 and delta[1] = -1. Year 1950 gets pop = 1, year 1951 gets pop = 0. Handled correctly.
Multiple Years Having Identical Maximum Population
e.g., [1950, 1960] and [1970, 1980]		 Returning a later year instead of the earliest. Comparison condition uses strictly greater than: if (runningPop > maxPop). Equal maximum populations do not overwrite earliestYear.
All Persons Born and Dying in Same Relative Intervals
e.g., [[1950, 2050], [1950, 2050]]		 Boundary array index out of bounds at index 100. Array size is 101 (indices 0 to 100). Year 2050 maps to index 2050 - 1950 = 100 without index exception.

Complexity Analysis Performance Metrics

Approach Category Time Complexity Space Complexity Performance Evaluation Rating
Approach 1: Brute Force Year Counting O(N * Y) O(Y) Auxiliary Sub-optimal. Iterates across lifespan range Y for every log entry N.
Approach 2: Event Sweep-Line Sorting O(N log N) O(N) Auxiliary General Range Choice. Works for unbounded year ranges, but sorting adds O(N log N) time overhead.
Approach 3: Line Sweep Difference Array O(N + Y) O(Y) = O(1) Auxiliary Optimal Production Standard. Takes advantage of bounded year space [1950, 2050]. Computes result in O(N) linear time and O(1) space.

LeetCode 904 Medium Master Edition

Fruit Into Baskets

An engineering manual analyzing subarray mapping, dynamic sliding windows, frequency tracking, and non-shrinking window optimization.

Problem Statement

You are visiting a farm that has a single row of fruit trees arranged from left to right. The trees are represented by an integer array fruits where fruits[i] is the type of fruit the i-th tree produces.

You want to collect as much fruit as possible. However, the owner has some strict rules:

  • You have two baskets, and each basket can only hold a single type of fruit. There is no limit on the amount of fruit each basket can hold.
  • Starting from any tree of your choice, you must pick exactly one fruit from every tree (including the start tree) while moving to the right. The picked fruits must fit in one of your baskets.
  • Once you reach a tree with fruit that cannot fit in your baskets, you must stop.

Given the integer array fruits, return the maximum number of fruits you can pick.

Constraints

  • 1 <= fruits.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= fruits[i] < fruits.length

Visualizing the Intent

Let's map out how the rules translate directly into finding contiguous subarray boundaries:

Input: fruits = [1, 2, 3, 2, 2] Valid Subarrays with at most 2 distinct fruit types: - Range [0, 1] -> [1, 2] (2 types: 1, 2) -> Length = 2 - Range [1, 4] -> [2, 3, 2, 2] (2 types: 2, 3) -> Length = 4 Maximum Fruits Collected = 4 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Input: fruits = [0, 1, 2, 2] Valid Subarrays: - Range [0, 1] -> [0, 1] (2 types) -> Length = 2 - Range [1, 3] -> [1, 2, 2] (2 types) -> Length = 3 Maximum Fruits Collected = 3

Core Realization: This problem is mathematically equivalent to finding the Longest Contiguous Subarray with at most 2 Distinct Elements!

Solutions Breakdown

Approach 1 - Brute Force (Nested Subarray Evaluation)

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (All Subarrays Inspection)

1. The Concept: Iterate through every possible starting position left of the orchard array. From each left, expand a right pointer right while keeping track of distinct fruit types using a Hash Set.

2. Stopping Condition: Once the Hash Set size exceeds 2, stop expanding for the current left and update the global maximum fruit count.

3. Why it Fails Constraints: Evaluating all N*(N+1)/2 subarrays requires O(N^2) time complexity. For N = 10^5, N^2 = 10^10 operations, leading to an immediate Time Limit Exceeded (TLE) error.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition: Har index left se shuru karke aage badho aur ek Set me fruit types store karte jao. Jaise hi Set ka size 2 se bada ho jaye (3 types ho jayein), us sub-array ki length calculate kar lo aur next left par jao. Isme O(N^2) time lagta hai jo large inputs ke liye bohot slow hai.

📋 Approach 1 Trace Profile

Input: fruits = [1, 2, 3, 2]

Initialize max_fruits = 0 • left = 0 (fruits[0] = 1): - right = 0: set = {1} -> length = 1 - right = 1: set = {1, 2} -> length = 2 - right = 2: set = {1, 2, 3} -> size (3) > 2! Stop right iteration. - max_fruits = max(0, 2) = 2 • left = 1 (fruits[1] = 2): - right = 1: set = {2} -> length = 1 - right = 2: set = {2, 3} -> length = 2 - right = 3: set = {2, 3} -> length = 3 - max_fruits = max(2, 3) = 3 • left = 2... Return max_fruits = 3

a) Source Code Implementation

class BruteForceSolution:
    def totalFruit(self, fruits: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(fruits)
        max_fruits = 0

        for left in range(n):
            basket = set()
            for right in range(left, n):
                basket.add(fruits[right])
                if len(basket) > 2:
                    break  # Exceeded 2 basket capacity limit
                max_fruits = max(max_fruits, right - left + 1)

        return max_fruits
class BruteForceSolution {
public:
    int totalFruit(vector<int>& fruits) {
        int n = fruits.size();
        int maxFruits = 0;

        for (int left = 0; left < n; ++left) {
            unordered_set<int> basket;
            for (int right = left; right < n; ++right) {
                basket.insert(fruits[right]);
                if (basket.size() > 2) break;
                maxFruits = max(maxFruits, right - left + 1);
            }
        }
        return maxFruits;
    }
};
class BruteForceSolution {
    public int totalFruit(int[] fruits) {
        int n = fruits.length;
        int maxFruits = 0;

        for (int left = 0; left < n; left++) {
            Set<Integer> basket = new HashSet<>();
            for (int right = left; right < n; right++) {
                basket.add(fruits[right]);
                if (basket.size() > 2) break;
                maxFruits = Math.max(maxFruits, right - left + 1);
            }
        }
        return maxFruits;
    }
}
var totalFruit = function(fruits) {
    const n = fruits.length;
    let maxFruits = 0;

    for (let left = 0; left < n; left++) {
        const basket = new Set();
        for (let right = left; right < n; right++) {
            basket.add(fruits[right]);
            if (basket.size > 2) break;
            maxFruits = Math.max(maxFruits, right - left + 1);
        }
    }
    return maxFruits;
};

Approach 2 - Dynamic Sliding Window with Frequency Map

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (Dynamic Range Contraction)

1. The Window Mechanics: Maintain a sliding window using two pointers, left and right, along with a Hash Map (or frequency array) freq tracking the count of each fruit type inside the current window.

2. Expansion Phase: Expand the right edge of the window by adding fruits[right] to freq.

3. Contraction Phase: If the number of distinct keys in freq exceeds 2, shrink the window from the left by decrementing freq[fruits[left]] and advancing left += 1. If a fruit's count reaches 0, delete it from the map completely.

4. Why Time Complexity is O(N): Both left and right pointers traverse the array from index 0 to N at most once. Each element is added and removed from the hash map once, ensuring linear O(N) execution.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition behind Sliding Window: Hum do pointers left aur right se ek window banate hain. Right pointer ko aage badhaate jao aur Frequency Map me fruit counts add karo. Jaise hi Map me **3 alag fruit types** ho jayein, left pointer ko tab tak aage badhao jab tak map me wapas **sirf 2 types** na reh jayein. Subarray ki max length track karte raho. Time complexity O(N) ho jaati hai.

📋 Approach 2 Line-by-Line Trace Profile

Input: fruits = [1, 2, 3, 2, 2]

Initialize: left = 0, max_fruits = 0, freq = {} • right = 0 (fruits[0] = 1): - freq = {1: 1} -> len(freq) = 1 <= 2 - max_fruits = max(0, 0 - 0 + 1) = 1 • right = 1 (fruits[1] = 2): - freq = {1: 1, 2: 1} -> len(freq) = 2 <= 2 - max_fruits = max(1, 1 - 0 + 1) = 2 • right = 2 (fruits[2] = 3): - freq = {1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 1} -> len(freq) = 3 > 2! INVALID WINDOW! - Shrink window from left: * decrement freq[fruits[0]] (1) -> freq[1] = 0 -> delete key 1 from freq! * left becomes 1 - freq is now {2: 1, 3: 1} -> len = 2. - max_fruits = max(2, 2 - 1 + 1) = 2 • right = 3 (fruits[3] = 2): - freq = {2: 2, 3: 1} -> len = 2 - max_fruits = max(2, 3 - 1 + 1) = 3 • right = 4 (fruits[4] = 2): - freq = {2: 3, 3: 1} -> len = 2 - max_fruits = max(3, 4 - 1 + 1) = 4 Final Maximum Fruits = 4

a) Source Code Implementation

from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def totalFruit(self, fruits: list[int]) -> int:
        freq = defaultdict(int)  # Map fruit_type -> count inside current window
        left = 0
        max_fruits = 0

        for right in range(len(fruits)):
            freq[fruits[right]] += 1  # Include right fruit in window

            # Shrink window from left until at most 2 distinct fruit types remain
            while len(freq) > 2:
                freq[fruits[left]] -= 1
                if freq[fruits[left]] == 0:
                    del freq[fruits[left]]  # Remove fruit type completely when count reaches 0
                left += 1

            max_fruits = max(max_fruits, right - left + 1)  # Update max length

        return max_fruits
class Solution {
public:
    int totalFruit(vector<int>& fruits) {
        unordered_map<int, int> freq;
        int left = 0;
        int maxFruits = 0;

        for (int right = 0; right < fruits.size(); ++right) {
            freq[fruits[right]]++;

            // Contraction phase
            while (freq.size() > 2) {
                freq[fruits[left]]--;
                if (freq[fruits[left]] == 0) {
                    freq.erase(fruits[left]);
                }
                left++;
            }

            maxFruits = max(maxFruits, right - left + 1);
        }

        return maxFruits;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int totalFruit(int[] fruits) {
        Map<Integer, Integer> freq = new HashMap<>();
        int left = 0;
        int maxFruits = 0;

        for (int right = 0; right < fruits.length; right++) {
            freq.put(fruits[right], freq.getOrDefault(fruits[right], 0) + 1);

            // Shrink window if map size > 2
            while (freq.size() > 2) {
                freq.put(fruits[left], freq.get(fruits[left]) - 1);
                if (freq.get(fruits[left]) == 0) {
                    freq.remove(fruits[left]);
                }
                left++;
            }

            maxFruits = Math.max(maxFruits, right - left + 1);
        }

        return maxFruits;
    }
}
var totalFruit = function(fruits) {
    const freq = new Map();
    let left = 0;
    let maxFruits = 0;

    for (let right = 0; right < fruits.length; right++) {
        freq.set(fruits[right], (freq.get(fruits[right]) || 0) + 1);

        // Shrink window
        while (freq.size > 2) {
            freq.set(fruits[left], freq.get(fruits[left]) - 1);
            if (freq.get(fruits[left]) === 0) {
                freq.delete(fruits[left]);
            }
            left++;
        }

        maxFruits = Math.max(maxFruits, right - left + 1);
    }

    return maxFruits;
};

Approach 3 - Optimal Solution: Non-Shrinking Sliding Window (O(1) Memory Array Map)

🧭 Deep Intuition Breakdown (Monotonic Window Expansion)

1. The Max-Window Insight: Since we only care about finding the maximum window size, we never actually need to shrink the window back down when it becomes invalid! Instead, we can simply let the window grow or shift forward without ever decreasing its max size!

How Non-Shrinking Window Operates: 1. If len(freq) <= 2: Window expands (right increments, left stays fixed). 2. If len(freq) > 2: Window shifts (right increments, left ALSO increments by 1 step). Result: The distance (right - left + 1) NEVER decreases! At the end of the array, the final window size (right - left + 1) IS the maximum valid size!

2. Direct Array Map Optimization:
Since fruit types are bounded within 0 <= fruits[i] < N, we can replace the dynamic Hash Map overhead with a fixed Direct Array / Frequency Table. We maintain an integer variable distinct_count tracking how many types currently have count > 0.

This eliminates map hash collisions and dynamic allocations, resulting in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space (or fixed O(N) array capacity)!

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition behind Non-Shrinking Window: Hume maximum length chahiye. Iska matlab jab window me 3 types aa jayein, toh window ko chhota karne ki jagah bas left ko bhi 1 step aage khiska do (shift window). Window ki size kabhi kam nahi hogi!

Hash Map ki jagah ek **Direct Frequency Array** use karo taaki Hash Overhead khatam ho jaye. Single pass me max window size automatically reserve ho jata hai.

📋 Full Trace Dry Run: Non-Shrinking Window Shift

Input: fruits = [1, 2, 3, 2, 2]

Initialize: left = 0, distinct_count = 0, freq_arr = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0] • right = 0 (fruit 1): - freq[1] becomes 1 -> distinct_count = 1 - distinct_count (1) <= 2 -> Valid window size = 1 • right = 1 (fruit 2): - freq[2] becomes 1 -> distinct_count = 2 - distinct_count (2) <= 2 -> Valid window size = 2 • right = 2 (fruit 3): - freq[3] becomes 1 -> distinct_count = 3 (> 2!) - Invalid! Do NOT shrink while-loop. Instead SHIFT LEFT BY 1: * freq[fruits[left]] (fruit 1) -= 1 -> freq[1] = 0 -> distinct_count becomes 2! * left += 1 (left becomes 1) - Window size remains = (2 - 1 + 1) = 2 • right = 3 (fruit 2): - freq[2] becomes 2 -> distinct_count = 2 - distinct_count (2) <= 2 -> Window expands! - Window size = (3 - 1 + 1) = 3 • right = 4 (fruit 2): - freq[2] becomes 3 -> distinct_count = 2 - distinct_count (2) <= 2 -> Window expands! - Window size = (4 - 1 + 1) = 4 Final Max Window Size = (4 - 0 + 1) = 4! (Note: left remained 1 at termination)

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def totalFruit(self, fruits: list[int]) -> int:
        freq = {}
        left = 0

        for right in range(len(fruits)):
            freq[fruits[right]] = freq.get(fruits[right], 0) + 1

            # HIGHLIGHT: If distinct types > 2, shift left pointer once (non-shrinking window)
            if len(freq) > 2:
                freq[fruits[left]] -= 1
                if freq[fruits[left]] == 0:
                    del freq[fruits[left]]
                left += 1

        # Maximum window size preserved till the end
        return len(fruits) - left
class Solution {
public:
    int totalFruit(vector<int>& fruits) {
        unordered_map<int, int> freq;
        int left = 0;

        for (int right = 0; right < fruits.size(); ++right) {
            freq[fruits[right]]++;

            // HIGHLIGHT: Non-shrinking window shift
            if (freq.size() > 2) {
                freq[fruits[left]]--;
                if (freq[fruits[left]] == 0) {
                    freq.erase(fruits[left]);
                }
                left++;
            }
        }

        return fruits.size() - left;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int totalFruit(int[] fruits) {
        Map<Integer, Integer> freq = new HashMap<>();
        int left = 0;

        for (int right = 0; right < fruits.length; right++) {
            freq.put(fruits[right], freq.getOrDefault(fruits[right], 0) + 1);

            // HIGHLIGHT: Single shift condition
            if (freq.size() > 2) {
                freq.put(fruits[left], freq.get(fruits[left]) - 1);
                if (freq.get(fruits[left]) == 0) {
                    freq.remove(fruits[left]);
                }
                left++;
            }
        }

        return fruits.length - left;
    }
}
var totalFruit = function(fruits) {
    const freq = new Map();
    let left = 0;

    for (let right = 0; right < fruits.length; right++) {
        freq.set(fruits[right], (freq.get(fruits[right]) || 0) + 1);

        // HIGHLIGHT: Shift window boundary
        if (freq.size > 2) {
            freq.set(fruits[left], freq.get(fruits[left]) - 1);
            if (freq.get(fruits[left]) === 0) {
                freq.delete(fruits[left]);
            }
            left++;
        }
    }

    return fruits.length - left;
};

Strategic Edge Cases Tracking Matrix

Edge Case Profile Algorithmic Risk Factor Mitigation Resolution Logic
Orchard Has <= 2 Total Fruit Types
e.g., [1, 1, 1] or [1, 2, 1, 2]		 Incomplete window expansion or premature contraction. Map size never exceeds 2. left remains at index 0 throughout. Returns full length N - 0 = N.
All Trees Different Types
e.g., [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]		 Window exceeding basket capacity at every step. Shift branch if (len(freq) > 2) triggers on every step after index 2, keeping max window size capped at 2. Correctly returns 2.
Single Element Array
e.g., [0]		 Array indexing or boundary underflow. Loop runs for index 0, map size is 1. Returns 1 - 0 = 1.

Complexity Analysis Performance Metrics

Approach Category Time Complexity Space Complexity Performance Evaluation Rating
Approach 1: Brute Force Subarrays O(N^2) O(1) Fails Constraints (TLE). Generates all N^2 subarrays. Unsuitable for N = 10^5.
Approach 2: Dynamic Shrinking Window O(N) O(1) Auxiliary Standard Production Solution. Both pointers advance linearly. Frequency map size is bounded by 3 keys max.
Approach 3: Non-Shrinking Window Shift O(N) O(1) Auxiliary Absolute Optimal Standard. Replaces contraction loop with a single branch check. Maximum iteration efficiency.

LeetCode 1 Easy Master Edition

Two Sum

An engineering manual analyzing pair matching paradigms, iterative search spaces, sorted-array two-pointer strategies, and linear hash table complement lookups.

Problem Statement

Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.

Constraints

  • 2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
  • -10^9 <= target <= 10^9
  • Only one valid answer exists.

Visualizing the Intent

Let's map out how complementary pairs pair together to form the target sum:

Input: nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9 Goal: Find indices i and j (where i != j) such that nums[i] + nums[j] == 9 Check pairs: - Index 0 (val = 2) + Index 1 (val = 7) = 2 + 7 = 9 (TARGET MATCH FOUND!) Output: [0, 1] --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Input: nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6 Complement Perspective: - For element at index 0 (val = 3): Needed complement = target - val = 6 - 3 = 3 - For element at index 1 (val = 2): Needed complement = target - val = 6 - 2 = 4 - For element at index 2 (val = 4): Needed complement = target - val = 6 - 4 = 2 (Found 2 at index 1!) Output: [1, 2]

Core Realization: For any number x at index i, we are searching for its unique required complement complement = target - x. The entire problem boils down to: How fast can we lookup whether complement has already been seen in the array?

Solutions Breakdown

Approach 1 - Brute Force (Nested Loop Pair Search)

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (Exhaustive Pair Scan)

1. The Concept: Test all possible pairs of elements using two nested loops. The outer loop selects the first element nums[i], and the inner loop checks every subsequent element nums[j] (where j > i).

2. Stopping Condition: Check if nums[i] + nums[j] == target. As soon as a match is discovered, return [i, j] immediately.

3. Why it is Sub-Optimal: Scanning all pairs requires evaluating N * (N - 1) / 2 combinations, leading to an O(N^2) time complexity. While simple and taking O(1) auxiliary space, it is unnecessarily slow for large arrays.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition: Sabse simple tarika yeh hai ki hum do nested loops chalayein. Outer loop pehla number nums[i] pick karta hai aur inner loop uske aage ke saare numbers nums[j] par jaakar check karta hai ki kya nums[i] + nums[j] == target hai. Isme saare pairs check karne padte hain isliye Time Complexity O(N^2) hoti hai.

📋 Approach 1 Trace Profile

Input: nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6

Outer loop i = 0 (nums[0] = 3): - Inner loop j = 1 (nums[1] = 2): 3 + 2 = 5 != 6 - Inner loop j = 2 (nums[2] = 4): 3 + 4 = 7 != 6 Outer loop i = 1 (nums[1] = 2): - Inner loop j = 2 (nums[2] = 4): 2 + 4 = 6 == 6 (MATCH!) Return [1, 2]

a) Source Code Implementation

class BruteForceSolution:
    def twoSum(self, nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        # Outer loop selects first element
        for i in range(n):
            # Inner loop checks remaining elements
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                if nums[i] + nums[j] == target:
                    return [i, j]
        return []
class BruteForceSolution {
public:
    vector<int> twoSum(vector<int>& nums, int target) {
        int n = nums.size();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            for (int j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {
                if (nums[i] + nums[j] == target) {
                    return {i, j};
                }
            }
        }
        return {};
    }
};
class BruteForceSolution {
    public int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {
        int n = nums.length;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
                if (nums[i] + nums[j] == target) {
                    return new int[]{i, j};
                }
            }
        }
        return new int[0];
    }
}
var twoSum = function(nums, target) {
    const n = nums.length;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (let j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (nums[i] + nums[j] === target) {
                return [i, j];
            }
        }
    }
    return [];
};

Approach 2 - Better Solution: Sorting with Two Pointers

🧭 Intuition Breakdown (Preserving Indices & Converging Pointers)

1. The Concept: On a sorted array, we can use two pointers (left at start, right at end) to find pair sums in O(N) time. If nums[left] + nums[right] < target, we increment left to increase the sum. If nums[left] + nums[right] > target, we decrement right to decrease the sum.

2. Preserving Original Indices: Sorting alters element indices! Because the problem asks for original indices, we must store each number alongside its original index as a tuple (number, original_index) before sorting.

3. Complexity Tradeoff: Sorting takes O(N log N) time and requires O(N) space for index tracking tuples. While faster than brute force, it is slightly slower than a hash table lookup.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition: Agar array sorted ho, toh Two-Pointer technique se pair sum bohot aasaani se mil jata hai (ek pointer shuruat me, ek aakhir me). Lekin kyuki hume original **indices** return karne hain, isliye pehle hum har element ko uske index ke saath pair karke save karte hain (val, original_idx) aur phir values ke base par sort karte hain. Sorting ki wajah se Time Complexity O(N log N) aur Space O(N) ho jaati hai.

📋 Approach 2 Line-by-Line Trace Profile

Input: nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6

Step 1: Pair elements with original indices indexed_nums = [(3, 0), (2, 1), (4, 2)] Step 2: Sort based on element values sorted = [(2, 1), (3, 0), (4, 2)] Step 3: Two Pointers (left = 0, right = 2) • Iteration 1: - sum = sorted[0].val + sorted[2].val = 2 + 4 = 6 - sum == target (6 == 6)! MATCH FOUND! - Original indices = [sorted[0].idx, sorted[2].idx] = [1, 2] Return [1, 2]

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def twoSum(self, nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]:
        # Store elements alongside their original indices
        indexed_nums = [(val, i) for i, val in enumerate(nums)]
        indexed_nums.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])  # Sort by value

        left, right = 0, len(nums) - 1

        while left < right:
            cur_sum = indexed_nums[left][0] + indexed_nums[right][0]
            if cur_sum == target:
                return [indexed_nums[left][1], indexed_nums[right][1]]
            elif cur_sum < target:
                left += 1
            else:
                right -= 1

        return []
class Solution {
public:
    vector<int> twoSum(vector<int>& nums, int target) {
        vector<pair<int, int>> indexedNums;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); ++i) {
            indexedNums.push_back({nums[i], i});
        }

        sort(indexedNums.begin(), indexedNums.end());

        int left = 0, right = nums.size() - 1;
        while (left < right) {
            int sum = indexedNums[left].first + indexedNums[right].first;
            if (sum == target) {
                return {indexedNums[left].second, indexedNums[right].second};
            } else if (sum < target) {
                left++;
            } else {
                right--;
            }
        }
        return {};
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {
        int[][] indexedNums = new int[nums.length][2];
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
            indexedNums[i][0] = nums[i];
            indexedNums[i][1] = i;
        }

        Arrays.sort(indexedNums, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));

        int left = 0, right = nums.length - 1;
        while (left < right) {
            int sum = indexedNums[left][0] + indexedNums[right][0];
            if (sum == target) {
                return new int[]{indexedNums[left][1], indexedNums[right][1]};
            } else if (sum < target) {
                left++;
            } else {
                right--;
            }
        }
        return new int[0];
    }
}
var twoSum = function(nums, target) {
    const indexedNums = nums.map((val, i) => [val, i]);
    indexedNums.sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]);

    let left = 0, right = nums.length - 1;
    while (left < right) {
        let sum = indexedNums[left][0] + indexedNums[right][0];
        if (sum === target) {
            return [indexedNums[left][1], indexedNums[right][1]];
        } else if (sum < target) {
            left++;
        } else {
            right--;
        }
    }
    return [];
};

Approach 3 - Optimal Solution: One-Pass Hash Map (Complement Lookup)

🧭 Deep Intuition Breakdown (Single-Pass Memory Lookup)

1. The Key Mathematical Equation:
For any current number nums[i], we require a complement number complement = target - nums[i].

2. One-Pass Hash Map Strategy:
Instead of adding all elements to a Hash Map first (which requires 2 passes), we check for the complement on the fly as we iterate:

  1. Maintain a Hash Map mapping element_value -> element_index.
  2. For each element nums[i] at index i:
    • Compute complement = target - nums[i].
    • Check if complement already exists as a key in our Hash Map!
    • If YES: We have found our matching pair! Return [hashmap[complement], i].
    • If NO: Store the current element and its index into the map: hashmap[nums[i]] = i and proceed to the next iteration.

3. Why One-Pass Works Cleanly for Duplicate Values:
If nums = [3, 3] and target = 6, at index 0 (val = 3), complement = 3 is not yet in the empty map, so 3 -> index 0 is inserted. At index 1 (val = 3), complement = 3 is found in the map at index 0! It immediately returns [0, 1] without key collision issues.

Hinglish Explanation (Main Ideas)

Intuition behind One-Pass Hash Map: Har number x ke liye, uske jodi-daarm (complement) ki value fix hoti hai: complement = target - x.

Hum array me ek hi baar (Single Pass) aage badhte hain. Har step par dekhte hain ki kya current number ka complement pehle se humare **Hash Map** me majood hai?
• Agar majood hai: Toh answer mil gaya! Direct unke indices [seen[complement], current_index] return kar do.
• Agar nahi hai: Toh current number aur uske index ko Map me save kar do (seen[nums[i]] = i).

Isse Time Complexity O(N) aur Space Complexity O(N) ho jati hai. Yeh sabse optimal tareeka hai!

📋 Full Line-by-Line Trace Dry Run 1: Standard Search

Input: nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9

Initialize: seen_map = {} ================================================================================= ITERATION 1: i = 0, num = 2 ================================================================================= • complement = target - num = 9 - 2 = 7 • Is complement (7) in seen_map? No! • Action: Save current number to seen_map seen_map[2] = 0 • Map State: {2: 0} ================================================================================= ITERATION 2: i = 1, num = 7 ================================================================================= • complement = target - num = 9 - 7 = 2 • Is complement (2) in seen_map? YES! • Index of complement = seen_map[2] = 0 • Current index = 1 • MATCH FOUND! Return [0, 1] Final Answer Returned: [0, 1]
📋 Full Line-by-Line Trace Dry Run 2: Duplicate Target Components

Input: nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6

Initialize: seen_map = {} • Iteration 0: i = 0, num = 3 - complement = 6 - 3 = 3 - 3 in seen_map? FALSE. - Insert seen_map[3] = 0 -> Map: {3: 0} • Iteration 1: i = 1, num = 2 - complement = 6 - 2 = 4 - 4 in seen_map? FALSE. - Insert seen_map[2] = 1 -> Map: {3: 0, 2: 1} • Iteration 2: i = 2, num = 4 - complement = 6 - 4 = 2 - 2 in seen_map? TRUE! (Found key 2 mapped to index 1) - Match! Return [seen_map[2], 2] -> [1, 2] Final Answer Returned: [1, 2]

a) Source Code Implementation

class Solution:
    def twoSum(self, nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]:
        seen = {}  # Hash Map: value -> index

        for i, num in enumerate(nums):
            complement = target - num  # Calculate required target pair

            # HIGHLIGHT: Check if complement exists in hash map
            if complement in seen:
                return [seen[complement], i]  # Return index of complement and current index

            seen[num] = i  # Record current value and index into map

        return []  # Fallback return (unreachable per constraints)
class Solution {
public:
    vector<int> twoSum(vector<int>& nums, int target) {
        unordered_map<int, int> seen;  // Hash map storing value -> index

        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); ++i) {
            int complement = target - nums[i];

            // HIGHLIGHT: Check hash map membership in O(1) avg
            if (seen.find(complement) != seen.end()) {
                return {seen[complement], i};
            }

            seen[nums[i]] = i;  // Store current value and index
        }

        return {};
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {
        Map<Integer, Integer> seen = new HashMap<>();  // Map value to index

        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
            int complement = target - nums[i];

            // HIGHLIGHT: Fast lookup check
            if (seen.containsKey(complement)) {
                return new int[]{seen.get(complement), i};
            }

            seen.put(nums[i], i);
        }

        return new int[0];
    }
}
var twoSum = function(nums, target) {
    const seen = new Map();  // Map storing value -> index

    for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
        const complement = target - nums[i];

        // HIGHLIGHT: Map lookup
        if (seen.has(complement)) {
            return [seen.get(complement), i];
        }

        seen.set(nums[i], i);
    }

    return [];
};

Strategic Edge Cases Tracking Matrix

Edge Case Profile Algorithmic Risk Factor Mitigation Resolution Logic
Identical Duplicate Values Forming Target
e.g., nums = [3, 3], target = 6		 Overwriting hash map key or using the same index twice. One-pass search checks seen.has(complement) before adding the current element to the map. Index 0 is checked against index 1 seamlessly without overwriting collision.
Negative Numbers and Negative Targets
e.g., nums = [-3, 4, 3, 90], target = 0		 Arithmetic subtraction sign bugs. Algebraic formula complement = target - num holds across negative ranges: 0 - (-3) = 3. Matches index of 3 smoothly.
Large Numbers (Range up to 10^9)
e.g., nums = [10^9, 10^9], target = 2*10^9		 Integer overflow during addition. Subtraction target - nums[i] or 64-bit integer handling (in languages like C++) avoids sum overflow bugs.

Complexity Analysis Performance Metrics

Approach Category Time Complexity Space Complexity Performance Evaluation Rating
Approach 1: Brute Force Nested Loops O(N^2) O(1) Sub-optimal. Evaluates all N*(N-1)/2 pairs. Too slow for large N.
Approach 2: Sorting with Two Pointers O(N log N) O(N) Better Choice. Faster than brute force, but requires extra space to preserve indices before sorting.
Approach 3: One-Pass Hash Map O(N) O(N) Absolute Production Standard. Single pass traversal over N elements. O(1) average hash map lookup time. Maximum execution speed.
