Largest Sum of Averages

Complete Technical & Mentorship Guide: Subarray partitioning, Prefix Sums, Top-Down Memoization vs Bottom-Up 2D/1D Dynamic Programming, and detailed dry runs.

1. Problem Statement & Core Concept

You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. You can partition the array into at most k non-empty adjacent subarrays.

The score of a partition is the sum of the averages of each subarray.

Return the maximum score you can achieve of all the possible partitions. Answers within 10^-6 of the actual answer will be accepted.

Problem Understanding: Example 1: nums = [9, 1, 2, 3, 9], k = 3 Partition Choices: Option A: [9], [1, 2, 3], [9] - Average of [9] = 9.0 - Average of [1, 2, 3] = (1 + 2 + 3) / 3 = 6 / 3 = 2.0 - Average of [9] = 9.0 - Total Score = 9.0 + 2.0 + 9.0 = 20.0 Option B: [9, 1], [2, 3], [9] - Average of [9, 1] = 5.0 - Average of [2, 3] = 2.5 - Average of [9] = 9.0 - Total Score = 5.0 + 2.5 + 9.0 = 16.5 Maximum Score is 20.0 (using exactly 3 partitions). Output: 20.0 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Example 2: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], k = 4 Output: 20.5

Core Mathematical Observations

  • Monotonic Partition Benefit: More partitions are always better or equal. The optimal score using at most k partitions is always achieved by using exactly k partitions (or n partitions if k >= n).
  • Contiguous Subarray Constraint: Subarrays must be adjacent segments; elements cannot be reordered or skipped.
  • Prefix Sum Optimization: The sum of any subarray nums[i..j] can be computed in O(1) time as prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]. Its average is (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1).

Constraints

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 100
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
  • 1 <= k <= nums.length

2. Approach 1: Recursive Brute Force (Exponential O(2^N))

🧭 Senior Mentor Explanation: The Decision Tree

Hey junior, when partitioning an array into k parts, think of placing cut-points one by one:

  • Suppose we are at starting index start and we have partitions_left remaining.
  • If partitions_left == 1, we have no more cuts to make! The remaining subarray from start to the end (n - 1) MUST be taken as a single chunk. We simply return its average.
  • Otherwise, we can place the next cut at any index end from start up to n - 1.
    • Take nums[start..end] as one partition (calculate its average).
    • Recursively find the best sum of averages for the rest: solve(end + 1, partitions_left - 1).
  • Take the maximum over all possible cut choices end!
Hinglish Explanation

Har step par hume decide karna hai ki current partition ko kahan tak expand karein. Hum start se lekar end tak ek chunk banate hain, uska average lete hain, aur baaki bache hue array ke liye k - 1 partitions ke saath recursive call laga dete hain. Kyonki same subproblems baar-baar repeat hoti hain, iska time exponential O(2^N) ho jata hai.

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 1)

  1. prefix = [0] * (n + 1): Precompute prefix sums so we can get any subarray sum in O(1) time.
  2. def average(i, j): return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1): Helper to calculate average of nums[i..j].
  3. def solve(start, k_left):: Recursive function defining the state: current start index and remaining partitions.
  4. if k_left == 1: return average(start, n - 1): Base case when only 1 partition is left.
  5. for end in range(start, n - k_left + 1):: Try every valid cut position that leaves enough elements for remaining partitions.
  6. max_score = max(max_score, average(start, end) + solve(end + 1, k_left - 1)): Pick the choice that maximizes total score.

Brute Force Implementation

class BruteForceSolution:
    def largestSumOfAverages(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> float:
        n = len(nums)
        prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(n):
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i]

        def avg(i, j):
            return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1)

        def solve(start, k_left):
            if k_left == 1:
                return avg(start, n - 1)

            best = 0.0
            for end in range(start, n - k_left + 1):
                best = max(best, avg(start, end) + solve(end + 1, k_left - 1))
            return best

        return solve(0, k)
class BruteForceSolution {
private:
    double avg(const vector<double>& prefix, int i, int j) {
        return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1.0);
    }

    double solve(int start, int kLeft, int n, const vector<double>& prefix) {
        if (kLeft == 1) return avg(prefix, start, n - 1);

        double best = 0.0;
        for (int end = start; end <= n - kLeft; ++end) {
            best = max(best, avg(prefix, start, end) + solve(end + 1, kLeft - 1, n, prefix));
        }
        return best;
    }

public:
    double largestSumOfAverages(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.size();
        vector<double> prefix(n + 1, 0.0);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];
        return solve(0, k, n, prefix);
    }
};
class BruteForceSolution {
    private double avg(double[] prefix, int i, int j) {
        return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1.0);
    }

    private double solve(int start, int kLeft, int n, double[] prefix) {
        if (kLeft == 1) return avg(prefix, start, n - 1);

        double best = 0.0;
        for (int end = start; end <= n - kLeft; end++) {
            best = Math.max(best, avg(prefix, start, end) + solve(end + 1, kLeft - 1, n, prefix));
        }
        return best;
    }

    public double largestSumOfAverages(int[] nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.length;
        double[] prefix = new double[n + 1];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];
        return solve(0, k, n, prefix);
    }
}
var largestSumOfAveragesBF = function(nums, k) {
    const n = nums.length;
    const prefix = new Array(n + 1).fill(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];

    function avg(i, j) {
        return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1);
    }

    function solve(start, kLeft) {
        if (kLeft === 1) return avg(start, n - 1);

        let best = 0.0;
        for (let end = start; end <= n - kLeft; end++) {
            best = Math.max(best, avg(start, end) + solve(end + 1, kLeft - 1));
        }
        return best;
    }

    return solve(0, k);
};

3. Approach 2: Top-Down Dynamic Programming with Memoization (O(K * N^2))

🧭 Senior Mentor Explanation: Overlapping Subproblems

Junior, notice that the state in our recursive function is completely defined by just two integers: (start, k_left).

Since start <= 100 and k_left <= 100, there are at most 100 * 100 = 10,000 unique states! The brute force recalculates the exact same (start, k_left) state millions of times across different cut combinations.

The Fix: Cache the result of memo[start][k_left] after computing it once. When called again, return the cached answer in O(1) time.

Hinglish Explanation

Total unique states sirf N * K hain. Hum ek 2D memoization table banayenge memo[start][k_left]. Jab bhi koi state pehli baar compute hogi, use table me store kar lenge. Agli baar wahi state aane par bina loop chalaye direct answer return kar denge.

Top-Down Memoization Implementation

from functools import lru_cache

class TopDownDPSolution:
    def largestSumOfAverages(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> float:
        n = len(nums)
        prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(n):
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i]

        def avg(i, j):
            return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1)

        @lru_cache(None)
        def solve(start: int, k_left: int) -> float:
            if k_left == 1:
                return avg(start, n - 1)

            best = 0.0
            for end in range(start, n - k_left + 1):
                score = avg(start, end) + solve(end + 1, k_left - 1)
                if score > best:
                    best = score
            return best

        return solve(0, k)
class TopDownDPSolution {
private:
    double avg(const vector<double>& prefix, int i, int j) {
        return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1.0);
    }

    double solve(int start, int kLeft, int n, const vector<double>& prefix, vector<vector<double>>& memo) {
        if (kLeft == 1) return avg(prefix, start, n - 1);
        if (memo[start][kLeft] > 0.0) return memo[start][kLeft];

        double best = 0.0;
        for (int end = start; end <= n - kLeft; ++end) {
            best = max(best, avg(prefix, start, end) + solve(end + 1, kLeft - 1, n, prefix, memo));
        }
        return memo[start][kLeft] = best;
    }

public:
    double largestSumOfAverages(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.size();
        vector<double> prefix(n + 1, 0.0);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];

        vector<vector<double>> memo(n, vector<double>(k + 1, 0.0));
        return solve(0, k, n, prefix, memo);
    }
};
class TopDownDPSolution {
    private double avg(double[] prefix, int i, int j) {
        return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1.0);
    }

    private double solve(int start, int kLeft, int n, double[] prefix, double[][] memo) {
        if (kLeft == 1) return avg(prefix, start, n - 1);
        if (memo[start][kLeft] > 0.0) return memo[start][kLeft];

        double best = 0.0;
        for (int end = start; end <= n - kLeft; end++) {
            best = Math.max(best, avg(prefix, start, end) + solve(end + 1, kLeft - 1, n, prefix, memo));
        }
        return memo[start][kLeft] = best;
    }

    public double largestSumOfAverages(int[] nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.length;
        double[] prefix = new double[n + 1];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];

        double[][] memo = new double[n][k + 1];
        return solve(0, k, n, prefix, memo);
    }
}
var largestSumOfAveragesMemo = function(nums, k) {
    const n = nums.length;
    const prefix = new Array(n + 1).fill(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];

    const memo = Array.from({ length: n }, () => new Array(k + 1).fill(0));

    function avg(i, j) {
        return (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]) / (j - i + 1);
    }

    function solve(start, kLeft) {
        if (kLeft === 1) return avg(start, n - 1);
        if (memo[start][kLeft] > 0) return memo[start][kLeft];

        let best = 0.0;
        for (let end = start; end <= n - kLeft; end++) {
            best = Math.max(best, avg(start, end) + solve(end + 1, kLeft - 1));
        }
        return memo[start][kLeft] = best;
    }

    return solve(0, k);
};

4. Approach 3: Optimal Bottom-Up Tabulation with 1D Space (O(K * N^2) Time, O(N) Space)

💡 Senior Mentor Explanation: Tabulation State Transition

Now let's build the iterative Bottom-Up DP table:

DP Definition: Let dp[i] be the maximum sum of averages for prefix nums[0..i-1] (i.e. the first i elements).

  1. Base Case (p = 1 partition):

    For each i from 1 to N, dp[i] = average(nums[0..i-1]) = prefix[i] / i.

  2. State Transitions (from p = 2 to k partitions):

    To compute the new DP state for i elements using p partitions, iterate over all possible previous split boundaries j (where p - 1 <= j < i):

    dp_new[i] = max_{j} ( dp_old[j] + average(nums[j..i-1]) )

    Where dp_old[j] is the best score partitioning the first j elements into p - 1 parts, and average(nums[j..i-1]) is the p-th partition chunk!

Hinglish Explanation

Bottom-Up me hum pehle 1 partition ka answer nikalte hain (har prefix ka simple average). Phir outer loop chalate hain p = 2 se k tak. Har naye partition ke liye hum check karte hain ki pichla cut j par lagane se max answer kya banega: dp[j] + average(j..i). Isse 2D table ko sirf 1D array me reduce kiya ja sakta hai!

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 3)

  1. dp = [0.0] * (n + 1): 1D array storing the max score for prefix lengths 0 to n.
  2. for i in range(1, n + 1): dp[i] = prefix[i] / i: Base initialization for p = 1 partition.
  3. for p in range(2, k + 1):: Loop through partition counts from 2 to k.
  4. for i in range(n, p - 1, -1):: Loop backward from n down to p (backward loop allows updating dp[i] in-place without overwriting previous dp[j] states!).
  5. for j in range(p - 1, i):: Test every valid cut point j.
  6. dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + (prefix[i] - prefix[j]) / (i - j)): Transition equation taking maximum score.
  7. return dp[n]: Return the optimal score for the full array of length n.

Optimal 1D Tabulation Implementation

class Solution:
    def largestSumOfAverages(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> float:
        n = len(nums)
        prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(n):
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i]

        # dp[i] represents max score for prefix of length i
        dp = [0.0] * (n + 1)

        # Base Case: 1 partition
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            dp[i] = prefix[i] / i

        # Transitions: from 2 to k partitions
        for p in range(2, k + 1):
            for i in range(n, p - 1, -1):
                for j in range(p - 1, i):
                    curr_avg = (prefix[i] - prefix[j]) / (i - j)
                    dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + curr_avg)

        return dp[n]
class Solution {
public:
    double largestSumOfAverages(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.size();
        vector<double> prefix(n + 1, 0.0);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];
        }

        vector<double> dp(n + 1, 0.0);
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
            dp[i] = prefix[i] / i;
        }

        for (int p = 2; p <= k; ++p) {
            for (int i = n; i >= p; --i) {
                for (int j = p - 1; j < i; ++j) {
                    double currAvg = (prefix[i] - prefix[j]) / (i - j);
                    dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + currAvg);
                }
            }
        }

        return dp[n];
    }
};
class Solution {
    public double largestSumOfAverages(int[] nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.length;
        double[] prefix = new double[n + 1];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];
        }

        double[] dp = new double[n + 1];
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            dp[i] = prefix[i] / i;
        }

        for (int p = 2; p <= k; p++) {
            for (int i = n; i >= p; i--) {
                for (int j = p - 1; j < i; j++) {
                    double currAvg = (prefix[i] - prefix[j]) / (i - j);
                    dp[i] = Math.max(dp[i], dp[j] + currAvg);
                }
            }
        }

        return dp[n];
    }
}
var largestSumOfAverages = function(nums, k) {
    const n = nums.length;
    const prefix = new Array(n + 1).fill(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];

    const dp = new Array(n + 1).fill(0);
    for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        dp[i] = prefix[i] / i;
    }

    for (let p = 2; p <= k; p++) {
        for (let i = n; i >= p; i--) {
            for (let j = p - 1; j < i; j++) {
                const currAvg = (prefix[i] - prefix[j]) / (i - j);
                dp[i] = Math.max(dp[i], dp[j] + currAvg);
            }
        }
    }

    return dp[n];
};

5. Boundary Traps & Floating-Point Precision Analysis

⚠️ Common Traps & Edge Cases

1. k == 1 (Single Partition):
Entire array is one partition. The answer is simply sum(nums) / len(nums). Handled immediately by the base case loop.

2. k == len(nums) (Every element in its own partition):
Every element forms a partition of size 1. The answer is simply the sum of all elements in the array: sum(nums).

3. Floating-Point Division in C++ / Java:
Dividing integer prefix sums by integer lengths truncates decimals! Always cast numerator or denominator to double (e.g. (prefix[i] - prefix[j]) / (double)(i - j)).

6. Detailed Dry Run Walkthroughs

📋 Dry Run 1: nums = [9, 1, 2, 3, 9], k = 3
Processing nums = [9, 1, 2, 3, 9] (n = 5), k = 3 Prefix Sums: prefix = [0, 9, 10, 12, 15, 24] --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Step 1: Base Case (p = 1 partition for all prefixes): dp[1] = 9/1 = 9.0 dp[2] = 10/2 = 5.0 dp[3] = 12/3 = 4.0 dp[4] = 15/4 = 3.75 dp[5] = 24/5 = 4.8 dp state (p=1): [0, 9.0, 5.0, 4.0, 3.75, 4.8] --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Step 2: p = 2 partitions: • i = 5 (elements [9,1,2,3,9]): - j = 1: dp[1] + avg(1..4) = 9.0 + (15/4 = 3.75) = 12.75 - j = 2: dp[2] + avg(2..4) = 5.0 + (14/3 = 4.66) = 9.66 - j = 3: dp[3] + avg(3..4) = 4.0 + (12/2 = 6.0) = 10.0 - j = 4: dp[4] + avg(4..4) = 3.75 + 9.0 = 12.75 dp[5] = max(4.8, 12.75, 9.66, 10.0, 12.75) = 12.75 • i = 4 (elements [9,1,2,3]): - j = 1: dp[1] + avg(1..3) = 9.0 + (6/3 = 2.0) = 11.0 - j = 2: dp[2] + avg(2..3) = 5.0 + (5/2 = 2.5) = 7.5 - j = 3: dp[3] + avg(3..3) = 4.0 + 3.0 = 7.0 dp[4] = max(3.75, 11.0, 7.5, 7.0) = 11.0 • i = 3 (elements [9,1,2]): - j = 1: dp[1] + avg(1..2) = 9.0 + (3/2 = 1.5) = 10.5 - j = 2: dp[2] + avg(2..2) = 5.0 + 2.0 = 7.0 dp[3] = max(4.0, 10.5, 7.0) = 10.5 • i = 2 (elements [9,1]): - j = 1: dp[1] + avg(1..1) = 9.0 + 1.0 = 10.0 dp[2] = 10.0 dp state (p=2): [0, 9.0, 10.0, 10.5, 11.0, 12.75] --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Step 3: p = 3 partitions: • i = 5 (elements [9,1,2,3,9]): - j = 2: dp[2] + avg(2..4) = 10.0 + (14/3 = 4.66) = 14.66 - j = 3: dp[3] + avg(3..4) = 10.5 + (12/2 = 6.0) = 16.5 - j = 4: dp[4] + avg(4..4) = 11.0 + (9/1 = 9.0) = 20.0 (Optimal!) dp[5] = max(12.75, 14.66, 16.5, 20.0) = 20.0 Final Output = dp[5] = 20.0
📋 Dry Run 2: Single Element Partitions — nums = [4, 1, 7], k = 3
Processing [4, 1, 7], k = 3: Since k == len(nums), each element forms its own partition: - [4] -> avg = 4.0 - [1] -> avg = 1.0 - [7] -> avg = 7.0 Total Score = 4.0 + 1.0 + 7.0 = 12.0 Final Output = 12.0

7. Complexity Analysis Performance Metrics

Approach Category Time Complexity Space Complexity Performance Evaluation Rating
Approach 1: Recursive Brute Force O(2^N) O(N) Call Stack Sub-optimal / TLE. Explores all partition combinations repeatedly.
Approach 2: Top-Down DP with Memoization O(K * N^2) O(K * N) Table Optimal Time. Solves each unique subproblem state exactly once.
Approach 3: Bottom-Up 1D Tabulation O(K * N^2) O(N) Auxiliary Absolute Production Standard. Iterative calculation with zero recursion overhead and 1D space optimization.

LeetCode 224 Hard Master Edition

Basic Calculator

Complete Technical & Mentorship Guide: Expression evaluation, unary negation handling, Shunting-Yard Infix-to-Postfix conversion vs Single-Stack contextual sign evaluation, and step-by-step dry runs.

1. Problem Statement & Core Concept

Given a string s representing a valid mathematical expression, implement a basic calculator to evaluate it, and return the result of the evaluation.

Note: You are not allowed to use any built-in function which evaluates strings as mathematical expressions, such as eval().

Evaluation Mechanics Visualization: Example 1: s = "1 + 1" - Direct arithmetic addition. Output: 2 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Example 2: s = " 2-1 + 2 " - Mixed additions and subtractions with redundant spaces. - (2 - 1) + 2 = 1 + 2 = 3. Output: 3 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Example 3: s = "(1+(4+5+2)-3)+(6+8)" - Nested parentheses precedence evaluation: 1. Inner (4 + 5 + 2) = 11 2. First outer group: (1 + 11 - 3) = 9 3. Second group: (6 + 8) = 14 4. Final expression: 9 + 14 = 23 Output: 23 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Example 4: s = "-(2 + 3)" or "- (3 - (-4))" - Expression starts with unary negation or has negative numbers in parentheses! Output for "-(2 + 3)": -5

Constraints & Structural Properties

  • 1 <= s.length <= 3 * 10^5
  • s consists of digits, '+', '-', '(', ')', and ' '.
  • s represents a valid expression.
  • '+' is not used as a unary operation (e.g., "+1" and "+(2 + 3)" are invalid).
  • '-' can be used as a unary operation (i.e., "-1" and "-(2 + 3)" are valid).
  • There will be no two consecutive operators in the input.
  • Every number and running calculation result fits in a standard 32-bit signed integer.

2. Approach 1: Classic Shunting-Yard Infix to Postfix (Reverse Polish Notation)

🧭 Senior Mentor Explanation: The Compiler Approach

Hey junior, the standard computer science way to parse any mathematical expression with parentheses is Dijkstra's Shunting-Yard Algorithm:

  1. Normalize Unary Negations: If a minus '-' appears at the very beginning of the string (e.g. "-2") or right after an open parenthesis '(' (e.g. "(-2+3)"), we insert a dummy 0 before it so it becomes a standard binary subtraction: "0-2".
  2. Convert Infix to Postfix (RPN): Using an operator stack, convert the expression into Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) where operators follow their operands (eliminating all parentheses).
  3. Evaluate Postfix Stack: Use an operand stack to evaluate the postfix tokens sequentially.
Hinglish Explanation

Yeh compiler design ka classic tarika hai. Pehle hum unary minus (jaise -5 ya (-3)) ke aage 0 laga dete hain taaki wo 0 - 5 ban jaye. Phir Shunting-Yard algorithm se parentheses hata kar Postfix (RPN) expression banate hain aur stack se evaluate kar lete hain. Yeh tarika generic hai aur *, / ke liye bhi extend ho sakta hai, par isme 2-3 passes lagte hain.

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 1)

  1. clean_s = []: Tokenize the input string and insert 0 before unary minuses (e.g., when - follows ( or is at start).
  2. ops, postfix = [], []: Shunting-yard conversion stacks for operators and output tokens.
  3. if token.isdigit(): postfix.append(int(token)): Push numbers directly into postfix stream.
  4. elif token == '(': ops.append('('): Push open parenthesis onto operator stack.
  5. elif token == ')': while ops[-1] != '(': postfix.append(ops.pop()); ops.pop(): Pop operators to postfix until matching ( is discarded.
  6. else: while ops and ops[-1] != '(': postfix.append(ops.pop()); ops.append(token): Standard precedence handling for + and -.
  7. eval_stack = []: Evaluate the resulting postfix tokens using standard RPN evaluation.

Shunting-Yard Implementation

class ShuntingYardSolution:
    def calculate(self, s: str) -> int:
        # Step 1: Tokenize and normalize unary operators
        tokens = []
        i = 0
        n = len(s)
        
        while i < n:
            if s[i] == ' ':
                i += 1
                continue
            if s[i].isdigit():
                num = 0
                while i < n and s[i].isdigit():
                    num = num * 10 + int(s[i])
                    i += 1
                tokens.append(num)
            else:
                # Unary minus check: if '-' occurs at start or after '('
                if s[i] == '-':
                    if not tokens or tokens[-1] == '(':
                        tokens.append(0)
                tokens.append(s[i])
                i += 1

        # Step 2: Convert Infix to Postfix (RPN)
        postfix = []
        ops = []
        for token in tokens:
            if isinstance(token, int):
                postfix.append(token)
            elif token == '(':
                ops.append(token)
            elif token == ')':
                while ops and ops[-1] != '(':
                    postfix.append(ops.pop())
                ops.pop()  # Discard '('
            else:  # '+' or '-'
                while ops and ops[-1] != '(':
                    postfix.append(ops.pop())
                ops.append(token)

        while ops:
            postfix.append(ops.pop())

        # Step 3: Evaluate Postfix
        eval_st = []
        for t in postfix:
            if isinstance(t, int):
                eval_st.append(t)
            else:
                b = eval_st.pop()
                a = eval_st.pop()
                if t == '+': eval_st.append(a + b)
                elif t == '-': eval_st.append(a - b)

        return eval_st[0]
class ShuntingYardSolution {
public:
    int calculate(string s) {
        stack<int> nums;
        stack<char> ops;
        int n = s.length();

        auto applyOp = [&]() {
            int b = nums.top(); nums.pop();
            int a = nums.top(); nums.pop();
            char op = ops.top(); ops.pop();
            if (op == '+') nums.push(a + b);
            if (op == '-') nums.push(a - b);
        };

        bool needZero = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            if (s[i] == ' ') continue;

            if (isdigit(s[i])) {
                long long val = 0;
                while (i < n && isdigit(s[i])) {
                    val = val * 10 + (s[i] - '0');
                    i++;
                }
                i--;
                nums.push(val);
                needZero = false;
            } else if (s[i] == '(') {
                ops.push('(');
                needZero = true;
            } else if (s[i] == ')') {
                while (ops.top() != '(') applyOp();
                ops.pop();
                needZero = false;
            } else { // '+' or '-'
                if (needZero && s[i] == '-') nums.push(0);
                while (!ops.empty() && ops.top() != '(') applyOp();
                ops.push(s[i]);
                needZero = true;
            }
        }
        while (!ops.empty()) applyOp();
        return nums.top();
    }
};
class ShuntingYardSolution {
    public int calculate(String s) {
        Deque<Integer> nums = new ArrayDeque<>();
        Deque<Character> ops = new ArrayDeque<>();
        boolean needZero = true;

        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
            char c = s.charAt(i);
            if (c == ' ') continue;

            if (Character.isDigit(c)) {
                int val = 0;
                while (i < s.length() && Character.isDigit(s.charAt(i))) {
                    val = val * 10 + (s.charAt(i) - '0');
                    i++;
                }
                i--;
                nums.push(val);
                needZero = false;
            } else if (c == '(') {
                ops.push('(');
                needZero = true;
            } else if (c == ')') {
                while (ops.peek() != '(') apply(nums, ops);
                ops.pop();
                needZero = false;
            } else {
                if (needZero && c == '-') nums.push(0);
                while (!ops.isEmpty() && ops.peek() != '(') apply(nums, ops);
                ops.push(c);
                needZero = true;
            }
        }
        while (!ops.isEmpty()) apply(nums, ops);
        return nums.pop();
    }

    private void apply(Deque<Integer> nums, Deque<Character> ops) {
        int b = nums.pop(), a = nums.pop();
        char op = ops.pop();
        nums.push(op == '+' ? a + b : a - b);
    }
}
var calculateShuntingYard = function(s) {
    const nums = [], ops = [];
    let needZero = true;

    const apply = () => {
        const b = nums.pop(), a = nums.pop(), op = ops.pop();
        nums.push(op === '+' ? a + b : a - b);
    };

    for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
        const c = s[i];
        if (c === ' ') continue;

        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
            let val = 0;
            while (i < s.length && s[i] >= '0' && s[i] <= '9') {
                val = val * 10 + Number(s[i++]);
            }
            i--;
            nums.push(val);
            needZero = false;
        } else if (c === '(') {
            ops.push('(');
            needZero = true;
        } else if (c === ')') {
            while (ops[ops.length - 1] !== '(') apply();
            ops.pop();
            needZero = false;
        } else {
            if (needZero && c === '-') nums.push(0);
            while (ops.length && ops[ops.length - 1] !== '(') apply();
            ops.push(c);
            needZero = true;
        }
    }
    while (ops.length) apply();
    return nums[0];
};

3. Approach 2: Optimal Single-Pass Sign & Context Stack (O(N) Time, O(N) Space)

💡 Senior Mentor Explanation: The State Preservation Insight

Junior, in LeetCode 224, there are only + and - operators (no multiplication or division precedence to worry about!).

Because addition and subtraction have the exact same precedence, we don't need complex operator queues! We can maintain a running result and a current sign (+1 or -1):

What about Parentheses '(' and ')'?

  • When we encounter an open parenthesis '(': A new local mathematical universe begins! We save the current state by pushing result and sign onto our stack, then reset result = 0 and sign = 1.
  • When we encounter a closing parenthesis ')': That local universe is finished! We pop the parent universe's sign and result, and combine them:
    result = popped_previous_result + (popped_previous_sign * current_sub_expression_result)
Hinglish Explanation

Kyonki yahan sirf + aur - hain, hume bas 2 cheezein track karni hain: running result aur current sign (+1 ya -1). Jab bhi '(' aaye, puraani calculation aur sign ko Stack me store karo aur naya bracket solve karna shuru karo. Jab ')' aaye, bracket ka result bahar nikal kar stack ke puraane result aur sign ke sath jod do!

Single-Pass Execution State Trace: Expression: s = "1 + (4 + 5 - 2) - 3" Initial: result = 0, sign = 1, stack = [] 1. char '1': current_num = 1 End of number -> result += 1 * 1 = 1 2. char '+': sign = +1 3. char '(': Save current universe: stack.push(result = 1), stack.push(sign = +1) Stack: [1, +1] Reset for bracket: result = 0, sign = +1 4. Inner "(4 + 5 - 2)": - Read 4 -> result = 0 + (+1 * 4) = 4 - Read '+' -> sign = +1 - Read 5 -> result = 4 + (+1 * 5) = 9 - Read '-' -> sign = -1 - Read 2 -> result = 9 + (-1 * 2) = 7 (Bracket evaluation is complete!) 5. char ')': Pop previous sign = +1 Pop previous result = 1 result = 1 + (+1 * 7) = 8 Stack: [] 6. char '-': sign = -1 7. char '3': result = 8 + (-1 * 3) = 5 Final Output = 5

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 2)

  1. stack = []: Stack storing tuples or pairs of [previous_result, previous_sign] before entering each parenthesis scope.
  2. result = 0, sign = 1, i = 0: Running accumulator, active sign multiplier (+1 for +, -1 for -), and string index pointer.
  3. if char.isdigit():: Parse multi-digit integers completely into num in a single inner while-loop: num = num * 10 + int(s[i]). Then immediately add to result: result += sign * num.
  4. elif char == '+': sign = 1: Update active operator sign for next incoming operand.
  5. elif char == '-': sign = -1: Update active operator sign to negative.
  6. elif char == '(':: Scope entrance! Push result then sign onto stack, and reset result = 0, sign = 1.
  7. elif char == ')':: Scope exit! Pop prev_sign, multiply with result, and add to popped prev_result: result = stack.pop() + stack.pop() * result.
  8. return result: Return final evaluated expression value.

Optimal Single-Pass Stack Implementation

class Solution:
    def calculate(self, s: str) -> int:
        stack = []
        result = 0
        sign = 1  # +1 for positive, -1 for negative
        i = 0
        n = len(s)

        while i < n:
            c = s[i]

            if c.isdigit():
                # Parse full multi-digit integer
                num = 0
                while i < n and s[i].isdigit():
                    num = num * 10 + int(s[i])
                    i += 1
                result += sign * num
                continue  # Skip increment because i was already advanced
            elif c == '+':
                sign = 1
            elif c == '-':
                sign = -1
            elif c == '(':
                # HIGHLIGHT: Push current accumulator and sign onto stack
                stack.append(result)
                stack.append(sign)
                result = 0
                sign = 1
            elif c == ')':
                # HIGHLIGHT: Complete bracket scope and merge with parent state
                prev_sign = stack.pop()
                prev_result = stack.pop()
                result = prev_result + prev_sign * result
            
            i += 1

        return result
class Solution {
public:
    int calculate(string s) {
        stack<int> st;
        long long result = 0;
        int sign = 1;
        int n = s.length();

        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            char c = s[i];

            if (isdigit(c)) {
                long long num = 0;
                while (i < n && isdigit(s[i])) {
                    num = num * 10 + (s[i] - '0');
                    i++;
                }
                i--;
                result += sign * num;
            } else if (c == '+') {
                sign = 1;
            } else if (c == '-') {
                sign = -1;
            } else if (c == '(') {
                st.push(result);
                st.push(sign);
                result = 0;
                sign = 1;
            } else if (c == ')') {
                int prevSign = st.top(); st.pop();
                int prevResult = st.top(); st.pop();
                result = prevResult + (long long)prevSign * result;
            }
        }

        return result;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int calculate(String s) {
        Deque<Integer> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
        int result = 0;
        int sign = 1;
        int n = s.length();

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            char c = s.charAt(i);

            if (Character.isDigit(c)) {
                int num = 0;
                while (i < n && Character.isDigit(s.charAt(i))) {
                    num = num * 10 + (s.charAt(i) - '0');
                    i++;
                }
                i--;
                result += sign * num;
            } else if (c == '+') {
                sign = 1;
            } else if (c == '-') {
                sign = -1;
            } else if (c == '(') {
                stack.push(result);
                stack.push(sign);
                result = 0;
                sign = 1;
            } else if (c == ')') {
                int prevSign = stack.pop();
                int prevResult = stack.pop();
                result = prevResult + prevSign * result;
            }
        }

        return result;
    }
}
var calculate = function(s) {
    const stack = [];
    let result = 0;
    let sign = 1;
    let i = 0;
    const n = s.length;

    while (i < n) {
        const c = s[i];

        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
            let num = 0;
            while (i < n && s[i] >= '0' && s[i] <= '9') {
                num = num * 10 + Number(s[i++]);
            }
            result += sign * num;
            continue;
        } else if (c === '+') {
            sign = 1;
        } else if (c === '-') {
            sign = -1;
        } else if (c === '(') {
            stack.push(result);
            stack.push(sign);
            result = 0;
            sign = 1;
        } else if (c === ')') {
            const prevSign = stack.pop();
            const prevResult = stack.pop();
            result = prevResult + prevSign * result;
        }
        i++;
    }

    return result;
};

4. Boundary Traps & Edge Case Analysis

⚠️ Common Traps & Edge Cases

1. Leading Unary Negation (e.g. s = "- (3 + 2)"):
Initially, result = 0. At char '-', sign = -1.
At '(', we push result = 0, then sign = -1.
Inside bracket, (3 + 2) = 5.
At ')': result = 0 + (-1 * 5) = -5. Handled smoothly without extra flags!

2. Redundant Whitespace Surrounding Numbers & Operators:
Expressions like " 1 + ( 2 - 3 ) " are ignored safely as spaces do not trigger any state changes.

3. Large Integer Overflows During String Digit Building:
Numbers can span up to 2147483647. In C++, building the number in long long prevents intermediate 32-bit integer overflow before multiplication by sign.

5. Detailed Dry Run Walkthroughs

📋 Dry Run 1: Nested Expression — s = "(1+(4+5+2)-3)+(6+8)"
Processing "(1+(4+5+2)-3)+(6+8)": Initial: result = 0, sign = 1, stack = [] • char '(': push result(0), push sign(1). stack = [0, 1]. Reset: result = 0, sign = 1 • char '1': result += 1 * 1 = 1 • char '+': sign = 1 • char '(': Inner bracket! Push result(1), push sign(1). stack = [0, 1, 1, 1]. Reset: result = 0, sign = 1 • char '4': result += 1 * 4 = 4 • char '+': sign = 1 • char '5': result += 1 * 5 = 9 • char '+': sign = 1 • char '2': result += 1 * 2 = 11 • char ')': Pop sign(1), pop result(1). result = 1 + 1 * 11 = 12. stack = [0, 1] • char '-': sign = -1 • char '3': result += -1 * 3 = 9 • char ')': Pop sign(1), pop result(0). result = 0 + 1 * 9 = 9. stack = [] • char '+': sign = 1 • char '(': Push result(9), push sign(1). stack = [9, 1]. Reset: result = 0, sign = 1 • char '6': result += 1 * 6 = 6 • char '+': sign = 1 • char '8': result += 1 * 8 = 14 • char ')': Pop sign(1), pop result(9). result = 9 + 1 * 14 = 23. stack = [] Final Output = 23
📋 Dry Run 2: Unary Negation with Subtraction — s = "- (3 - (-4))"
Processing "- (3 - (-4))": Initial: result = 0, sign = 1, stack = [] • char '-': sign = -1 • char '(': Push result(0), push sign(-1). stack = [0, -1]. Reset: result = 0, sign = 1 • char '3': result += 1 * 3 = 3 • char '-': sign = -1 • char '(': Push result(3), push sign(-1). stack = [0, -1, 3, -1]. Reset: result = 0, sign = 1 • char '-': sign = -1 • char '4': result += -1 * 4 = -4 • char ')': Pop sign(-1), pop result(3). result = 3 + (-1 * -4) = 3 + 4 = 7. stack = [0, -1] • char ')': Pop sign(-1), pop result(0). result = 0 + (-1 * 7) = -7. stack = [] Final Output = -7

6. Complexity Analysis Performance Metrics

Approach Category Time Complexity Space Complexity Pass Count Performance Evaluation Rating
Approach 1: Shunting-Yard (Infix to Postfix) O(N) O(N) Auxiliary 3 Passes (Tokenize, Convert, Evaluate) Compiler General Standard. Flexible for expanding to *, /, ^, but has extra queue/stack conversion passes.
Approach 2: Sign & Context Stack (Optimal) O(N) O(N) Auxiliary 1 Pass (Single Stream Scan) Absolute Production Standard. Evaluates the entire string in a single linear pass with minimal CPU cycles and constant register operations.

SQL Learning Series: Fundamentals to Interview Level

Database Constraints, Schema Evolution & Maintenance

1. What is it?

📖 The Origin Story: The Live Production Upgrade Crisis Imagine your e-commerce application has 5,000,000 customers. One day, a buggy backend deployment attempts to write negative prices, duplicate emails, and orphan orders for deleted user IDs into the database. Without database-level Constraints, the database gets corrupted instantly. Six months later, the business wants to add two-factor authentication (2FA) and phone numbers. You cannot drop and recreate the table because doing so destroys all 5 million active users! You need to evolve live table blueprints without downtime using ALTER, MODIFY, and CHANGE. And when 20 million temporary log rows need to be cleared in milliseconds without destroying the schema, you execute TRUNCATE.

Simple Explanation

Database Constraints are declarative security rules enforced directly by the database engine on columns and tables to maintain Data Integrity (validity, uniqueness, and consistency).

  • PRIMARY KEY: Uniquely identifies each record. It is mandatory, non-null, and automatically indexed.
  • FOREIGN KEY: Links child tables to a parent table, ensuring referential integrity and preventing orphan data.
  • UNIQUE: Enforces that all values in a column are distinct from one another across all rows.
  • CHECK: Validates that data satisfies a specific boolean condition before disk writes (e.g., price > 0).
  • DEFAULT: Automatically injects a fallback value if an INSERT statement omits that field.
  • AUTO_INCREMENT / SERIAL / IDENTITY: Automatically increments sequence values for Primary Keys without manual arithmetic.
  • CASCADE (ON DELETE / ON UPDATE): Automatically cascades deletions or modifications from a parent row to child rows.

Schema Evolution & Maintenance Commands modify the table structure dynamically or reset data:

  • ALTER TABLE: Adds, drops, or reconfigures columns and constraints on an existing table with live data.
  • MODIFY: Changes a column's data type, size, or constraint rules without renaming it (MySQL/Oracle; PostgreSQL uses ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE).
  • CHANGE: Renames a column AND modifies its data type/constraints in a single operation (MySQL dialect).
  • TRUNCATE: High-speed DDL command that deallocates all data pages from disk, resetting auto-increment sequences to 1 while leaving the structural blueprint intact.
💡 Hinglish Summary: Core Idea Constraints database ke guards hote hain jo duplicate, missing, ya invalid data ko disk par likhne se rokte hain (jaise negative salary ya duplicate phone number). CASCADE parent data delete hone par related child records ko manage karta hai. Jab live table me bina data lose kiye naye columns add karne hon ya datatype badalna ho, tab ALTER, MODIFY, aur CHANGE use hote hain. Aur jab table ke structure ko zinda rakh kar saara data instantly wipe karke auto-increment 1 par reset karna ho, tab TRUNCATE use hota hai.

2. Syntax & Dialect Blueprint

1. Defining Constraints on Table Creation

-- Parent Entity: Departments
CREATE TABLE departments (
    dept_id INT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    dept_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Child Entity: Employees with Cascading Foreign Key
CREATE TABLE employees (
    emp_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    full_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
    age INT CHECK (age >= 18 AND age <= 65),
    salary DECIMAL(10,2) DEFAULT 30000.00 CHECK (salary > 0),
    department_id INT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_department
        FOREIGN KEY (department_id) 
        REFERENCES departments(dept_id)
        ON DELETE CASCADE
        ON UPDATE CASCADE
);

2. Schema Evolution Syntax Across Dialects

Operation MySQL Syntax PostgreSQL Syntax
Add Column ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN phone VARCHAR(15); ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN phone VARCHAR(15);
Drop Column ALTER TABLE employees DROP COLUMN phone; ALTER TABLE employees DROP COLUMN phone;
Modify Type / Size ALTER TABLE employees MODIFY salary DECIMAL(12,2); ALTER TABLE employees ALTER COLUMN salary TYPE DECIMAL(12,2);
Rename & Redefine ALTER TABLE employees CHANGE full_name name VARCHAR(120); ALTER TABLE employees RENAME COLUMN full_name TO name;
Add Constraint ALTER TABLE employees ADD CONSTRAINT chk_sal CHECK (salary > 0); ALTER TABLE employees ADD CONSTRAINT chk_sal CHECK (salary > 0);
TRUNCATE (Fast Wipe) TRUNCATE TABLE employees; TRUNCATE TABLE employees RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;

3. Dataset Setup for Examples

Table 1: departments (Parent Entity)

dept_id (PK) dept_name (UNIQUE) location (DEFAULT)
1EngineeringNew York
2SalesChicago
3MarketingRemote

Table 2: employees (Child Entity)

emp_id (PK) full_name email (UNIQUE) age (CHECK) salary (CHECK) department_id (FK)
101Alice Stonealice@corp.com2995000.001
102Bob Millerbob@corp.com3562000.002
103Charlie Daycharlie@corp.com42110000.001

4. Individual Operator & Command Examples (Exhaustive List)

1. Primary Key: PRIMARY KEY

Requirement: Prevent duplicate IDs and reject missing identifiers.

-- Attempting duplicate ID insert
INSERT INTO employees (emp_id, full_name, email, age, salary, department_id)
VALUES (101, 'Dave Wilson', 'dave@corp.com', 30, 70000.00, 2);
-- ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "employees_pkey"

2. Uniqueness Constraint: UNIQUE

Requirement: Guarantee every employee has a distinct email address.

-- Attempting duplicate email
INSERT INTO employees (emp_id, full_name, email, age, salary, department_id)
VALUES (104, 'Alice Junior', 'alice@corp.com', 22, 50000.00, 1);
-- ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "employees_email_key"

3. Value Validation: CHECK

Requirement: Reject negative salaries and underage workers.

-- Attempting invalid age & negative salary
INSERT INTO employees (emp_id, full_name, email, age, salary, department_id)
VALUES (105, 'Kevin', 'kevin@corp.com', 16, -500.00, 1);
-- ERROR: new row violates check constraint "employees_age_check"

4. Fallback Values: DEFAULT

Requirement: Automatically inject $30,000 when salary is omitted during insertion.

INSERT INTO employees (emp_id, full_name, email, age, department_id)
VALUES (106, 'Eva Green', 'eva@corp.com', 28, 2);

SELECT emp_id, full_name, salary FROM employees WHERE emp_id = 106;
emp_idfull_namesalary
106Eva Green30000.00

5. Auto-Generating Keys: AUTO_INCREMENT / SERIAL

Requirement: Automatically generate next sequential department ID.

INSERT INTO departments (dept_name) VALUES ('Human Resources');
SELECT dept_id, dept_name FROM departments WHERE dept_name = 'Human Resources';
dept_iddept_name
4Human Resources

6. Referential Link & Cascading: FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE

Requirement: Deleting a department automatically deletes all child employee records linked to it.

DELETE FROM departments WHERE dept_id = 2; -- Deletes Sales
SELECT emp_id, full_name, department_id FROM employees;
emp_idfull_namedepartment_id
101Alice Stone1
103Charlie Day1

7. Evolving Table Structure: ALTER TABLE ADD / DROP

Requirement: Add an active status column and drop an obsolete column.

-- Add new column
ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE;

-- Drop column
ALTER TABLE employees DROP COLUMN is_active;

8. Column Type Modification: MODIFY vs CHANGE

Requirement: Expand column size (MODIFY) vs rename and change column type (CHANGE).

-- MySQL: MODIFY to expand data type
ALTER TABLE employees MODIFY full_name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL;

-- MySQL: CHANGE to rename and redefine
ALTER TABLE employees CHANGE full_name legal_name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL;

-- PostgreSQL equivalent:
ALTER TABLE employees ALTER COLUMN full_name TYPE VARCHAR(150);
ALTER TABLE employees RENAME COLUMN full_name TO legal_name;

9. Rapid Data Reset: TRUNCATE TABLE

Requirement: Instantly wipe all rows, reset identity counter, but preserve table schema.

TRUNCATE TABLE employees RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees;
count
0

5. Deep-Dive Comparison: TRUNCATE vs DELETE vs DROP

Feature / Property DELETE TRUNCATE DROP
SQL Taxonomy Group DML (Data Manipulation) DDL (Data Definition) DDL (Data Definition)
Disk Storage Action Scans row-by-row, writes individual undo logs for every deleted row. Deallocates data pages directly from storage in bulk. Deallocates data pages AND removes schema metadata from catalog.
Conditional Filtering (WHERE) YES. Can delete specific rows: WHERE id = 5. NO. Wipes all rows unconditionally. NO. Eradicates the entire table entity.
Auto-Increment Counter Does NOT reset the sequence counter. Resets sequence counter back to seed (1). Completely erased.
Schema State After Command Schema remains intact. Schema remains intact (empty table). Schema is completely removed.
💡 Hinglish Summary: Core Differences
  • DELETE: Row-by-row delete karta hai (DML), WHERE condition laga sakte hain, slow hota hai, auto-increment counter reset nahi hota.
  • TRUNCATE: Poora data ek jhatke me saaf kar deta hai (DDL), bohot fast hota hai, schema zinda rehta hai, aur auto-increment 1 se reset ho jata hai.
  • DROP: Table ka data aur uska poora structure (blueprint) dono disk aur memory se permanent delete kar deta hai.

6. Common Mistakes & Production Hazards

1. The Primary Key vs Unique Key Trap

  • A table can have only one PRIMARY KEY, but multiple UNIQUE keys.
  • PRIMARY KEY strictly forbids NULL values. UNIQUE columns can accept NULL values (because missing data does not conflict with uniqueness).
  • In most engines, a Primary Key automatically creates a Clustered Index (dictating physical disk row order), while a Unique Key creates a Non-Clustered Index.

2. Adding `NOT NULL` to a Table with Existing NULL Data

If existing rows have NULL values, running ALTER TABLE employees ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; fails immediately. You must backfill existing NULL rows with a fallback value before adding the constraint.

3. Downsizing Column Lengths in Production

Shrinking VARCHAR(100) to VARCHAR(20) when rows contain 50-character strings throws a fatal truncation error. Always verify string max lengths before altering data types.

7. Practice Problems (30 Questions)

Solve these questions on paper or in your SQL editor to build production-ready muscle memory. Solutions are withheld for practice.

Level 1: Constraints Definition (1–10)

  1. Create a table named roles with an auto-incrementing role_id as Primary Key and a non-null role_name.
  2. Create a customers table where phone_number is enforced to be UNIQUE.
  3. Define a products table with a price column that uses a CHECK constraint to prevent negative or zero prices.
  4. Create an accounts table where is_active defaults to TRUE and created_at defaults to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
  5. Write a query to create a table with a Composite Primary Key consisting of two columns: student_id and course_id.
  6. Create a users table where username cannot be null and must be unique.
  7. Define a vehicles table with a CHECK constraint ensuring manufacturing_year >= 1900.
  8. Create an inventory table where stock_quantity defaults to 0 and cannot be negative.
  9. Write a query to create a categories table with a self-referencing foreign key column parent_category_id.
  10. Define a payments table where payment_status is constrained via CHECK to only allow 'PENDING', 'COMPLETED', or 'FAILED'.

Level 2: Referential Integrity & Cascades (11–20)

  1. Create an orders table that links to customers(customer_id) using a Foreign Key constraint named fk_customer.
  2. Write the table definition for order_items with an ON DELETE CASCADE rule pointing to orders(order_id).
  3. Create a student_profiles table where deleting a student sets the student_id foreign key in profiles to SET NULL.
  4. Write an INSERT statement that intentionally fails due to a Foreign Key constraint violation, and explain the error.
  5. Create an invoices table with a foreign key that enforces ON UPDATE CASCADE when customer IDs are modified.
  6. Write two related tables: authors and books, ensuring a book cannot exist without an author (Foreign Key with NOT NULL).
  7. Create a posts table and a comments table. Configure comments such that deleting a post automatically deletes all its associated comments.
  8. Explain the difference between ON DELETE RESTRICT and ON DELETE NO ACTION.
  9. Write a table with a Composite Foreign Key referencing a Composite Primary Key in another table.
  10. Write the complete DDL to establish a Many-to-Many relationship between students and courses using an enrollment junction table with proper cascading constraints.

Level 3: Schema Evolution & Maintenance (21–30)

  1. Write an ALTER TABLE query to add an email VARCHAR(100) column to an existing customers table.
  2. Write a query to drop the age column from a users table.
  3. Write the SQL to rename the column phone to mobile_number in a contacts table.
  4. Write a query to modify the data type of salary in an employees table from INT to DECIMAL(12,2).
  5. Write a query to add a UNIQUE constraint to an existing column national_id in an employees table.
  6. Write the command to add a DEFAULT 'pending' value to the status column in an orders table using ALTER TABLE.
  7. Write the command to remove an existing check constraint chk_price from a products table.
  8. Write the PostgreSQL command to truncate a table invoices and simultaneously reset its identity sequence counter back to 1.
  9. Explain what happens if you run DELETE FROM logs; vs TRUNCATE TABLE logs; when the next insert happens.
  10. Write an ALTER TABLE query that adds two columns (created_at TIMESTAMP and updated_at TIMESTAMP) in a single SQL statement.

8. Quick Revision Cheat Sheet

  • Constraints: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT, NOT NULL.
  • Primary Key Rules: 1 per table, unique, strictly non-null, creates clustered index.
  • Unique Key Rules: Multiple allowed, permits NULL values, creates non-clustered index.
  • Cascade Options: CASCADE (propagates), RESTRICT / NO ACTION (blocks), SET NULL (orphans to null).
  • Add Column: ALTER TABLE tbl ADD COLUMN col_name datatype [constraints];
  • Drop Column: ALTER TABLE tbl DROP COLUMN col_name;
  • Modify Column: MODIFY (MySQL) / ALTER COLUMN TYPE (PostgreSQL).
  • Rename & Redefine: CHANGE (MySQL) / RENAME COLUMN (PostgreSQL).
  • Truncate vs Delete: TRUNCATE is DDL (fast page deallocation, resets sequences, no WHERE). DELETE is DML (slower row-by-row logging, supports WHERE).

9. What SQL Topic Should You Learn Next?

You should learn Data Mutation & Conditional Operations (`UPDATE`, conditional `DELETE`, and `MERGE / UPSERT`) next.

Why?

Now that your tables have solid structural rules (`CONSTRAINTS`), can evolve dynamically (`ALTER`), and can be reset safely (`TRUNCATE`), the next step is mastering row-level data mutations (`UPDATE ... SET`) and precision row deletions (`DELETE ... WHERE`) without causing constraint violations in production.

Range Addition

Complete Technical & Mentorship Guide: Subarray mutation overhead, the Difference Array Pattern (O(1) range updates), Prefix Sum accumulation, and detailed dry runs.

1. Problem Statement & Core Concept

You are given an integer length and an array updates where updates[i] = [startIdx_i, endIdx_i, inc_i].

You have an array arr of length length with all zeros initially.

Apply all updates[i] sequentially. Each updates[i] adds the increment inc_i to all elements in the index range [startIdx_i, endIdx_i] inclusive.

Return the modified array arr after applying all updates.

Problem Walkthrough: Input: length = 5, updates = [[1, 3, 2], [2, 4, 3], [0, 2, -2]] Initial Array (size 5): [ 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 ] 1. Apply update [1, 3, 2] (Add +2 from index 1 to 3): [ 0, 2, 2, 2, 0 ] 2. Apply update [2, 4, 3] (Add +3 from index 2 to 4): [ 0, 2, 5, 5, 3 ] 3. Apply update [0, 2, -2] (Add -2 from index 0 to 2): [-2, 0, 3, 5, 3 ] Final Output: [-2, 0, 3, 5, 3]

Constraints

  • 1 <= length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= updates.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= startIdx_i <= endIdx_i < length
  • -1000 <= inc_i <= 1000

2. Approach 1: Naive Range Iteration (O(K * N) Time)

🧭 Senior Mentor Explanation: The Direct Mutation Idea

Hey junior, the most direct way to solve this problem is simply to do what the prompt literally asks:

  1. Initialize an array of zeros of size length.
  2. For every operation [start, end, inc] in updates, run a loop from start to end and add inc to each index: arr[i] += inc.
Hinglish Explanation

Sabse seedha tarika yeh hai ki hum har update query ke liye loop chalayein start se end tak aur har element me inc add kar dein. Lekin agar K = 10^4 updates hain aur array ka size N = 10^5 hai, toh total operations 10^4 * 10^5 = 10^9 ho jayenge, jisse code TLE (Time Limit Exceeded) dega.

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 1)

  1. arr = [0] * length: Allocate initial array filled with zeros.
  2. for start, end, inc in updates:: Iterate through every update instruction tuple.
  3. for i in range(start, end + 1): arr[i] += inc: Iterate through all indices inside the inclusive range [start, end] and add inc.
  4. return arr: Return the final mutated array.

Naive Implementation

class NaiveSolution:
    def getModifiedArray(self, length: int, updates: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        arr = [0] * length
        # O(K * N) Naive update for each query
        for start, end, inc in updates:
            for i in range(start, end + 1):
                arr[i] += inc
        return arr
class NaiveSolution {
public:
    vector<int> getModifiedArray(int length, vector<vector<int>>& updates) {
        vector<int> arr(length, 0);
        for (const auto& u : updates) {
            int start = u[0], end = u[1], inc = u[2];
            for (int i = start; i <= end; ++i) {
                arr[i] += inc;
            }
        }
        return arr;
    }
};
class NaiveSolution {
    public int[] getModifiedArray(int length, int[][] updates) {
        int[] arr = new int[length];
        for (int[] u : updates) {
            int start = u[0], end = u[1], inc = u[2];
            for (int i = start; i <= end; i++) {
                arr[i] += inc;
            }
        }
        return arr;
    }
}
var getModifiedArrayNaive = function(length, updates) {
    const arr = new Array(length).fill(0);
    for (const [start, end, inc] of updates) {
        for (let i = start; i <= end; i++) {
            arr[i] += inc;
        }
    }
    return arr;
};

3. Approach 2: Optimal Difference Array & Prefix Sum (O(N + K) Time, O(1) Auxiliary Space)

💡 Senior Mentor Explanation: The Difference Array & Prefix Sum Magic

Junior, can we apply each range update in O(1) Constant Time instead of O(N)?

Yes! This is the classic Difference Array Pattern:

Suppose you want to add inc to every element from start to end:

  • If we perform a running prefix sum later, adding +inc at index start will automatically propagate +inc to every element to the right of start!
  • To stop this propagation past end, we place a cancellation marker -inc at index end + 1!
Difference Array Rules for range [start, end] with value +inc: 1. diff[start] += inc (Starts adding +inc from index 'start' onwards during prefix accumulation) 2. If end + 1 < length: diff[end + 1] -= inc (Cancels out the +inc effect for indices beyond 'end') Each range update is performed in strictly O(1) time! After all K updates are marked, ONE single Prefix Sum pass reconstructs the entire array in O(N) time!
Hinglish Explanation

Difference Array ka concept yeh hai ki hum pure range me loop chalane ke bajaye sirf 2 boundary markers lagate hain: diff[start] += inc aur diff[end + 1] -= inc. Jab hum aakhri me prefix sum (cumulative sum) nikalenge, toh start se lekar end tak sabhi elements me automatic +inc add ho jayega aur end + 1 par pahunchte hi wo cancel ho jayega. Isse K updates sirf O(K) time me ho jate hain!



Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 2)

  1. diff = [0] * length: Initialize the difference array of size length filled with 0s.
  2. for start, end, inc in updates:: Loop through each update query.
  3. diff[start] += inc: Mark the start of the increment interval.
  4. if end + 1 < length: diff[end + 1] -= inc: If end + 1 is within bounds, place the cancellation marker.
  5. for i in range(1, length): diff[i] += diff[i - 1]: Compute the running prefix sum in-place from left to right. This converts boundary markers into the actual values!
  6. return diff: Return the final mutated array.

Optimal Difference Array Implementation

class Solution:
    def getModifiedArray(self, length: int, updates: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        diff = [0] * length

        # Step 1: Apply O(1) Difference Array markers for each update
        for start, end, inc in updates:
            diff[start] += inc
            if end + 1 < length:
                diff[end + 1] -= inc

        # Step 2: Compute running prefix sum in-place O(N)
        for i in range(1, length):
            diff[i] += diff[i - 1]

        return diff
class Solution {
public:
    vector<int> getModifiedArray(int length, vector<vector<int>>& updates) {
        vector<int> diff(length, 0);

        // Step 1: O(1) Boundary Markers
        for (const auto& u : updates) {
            int start = u[0], end = u[1], inc = u[2];
            diff[start] += inc;
            if (end + 1 < length) {
                diff[end + 1] -= inc;
            }
        }

        // Step 2: Prefix sum accumulation
        for (int i = 1; i < length; ++i) {
            diff[i] += diff[i - 1];
        }

        return diff;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public int[] getModifiedArray(int length, int[][] updates) {
        int[] diff = new int[length];

        // Step 1: O(1) Boundary Markers
        for (int[] u : updates) {
            int start = u[0], end = u[1], inc = u[2];
            diff[start] += inc;
            if (end + 1 < length) {
                diff[end + 1] -= inc;
            }
        }

        // Step 2: Prefix sum accumulation
        for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
            diff[i] += diff[i - 1];
        }

        return diff;
    }
}
var getModifiedArray = function(length, updates) {
    const diff = new Array(length).fill(0);

    // Step 1: O(1) Boundary Markers
    for (const [start, end, inc] of updates) {
        diff[start] += inc;
        if (end + 1 < length) {
            diff[end + 1] -= inc;
        }
    }

    // Step 2: Prefix sum accumulation
    for (let i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        diff[i] += diff[i - 1];
    }

    return diff;
};

4. Boundary Traps & Edge Case Analysis

⚠️ Common Traps & Edge Cases

1. Out-of-Bounds Cancellation (end == length - 1):
When an update covers the very end of the array (end = length - 1), end + 1 = length is out of bounds! We do not place a cancellation marker because the increment effect naturally runs to the end of the array without needing to be stopped. The if end + 1 < length: check guards against index-out-of-range errors.

2. Negative Increments (inc < 0):
Subtracting values works naturally: diff[start] += (-5) and diff[end + 1] -= (-5) (which becomes +5, canceling the negative subtraction).

3. Single Element Range (start == end):
diff[start] += inc and diff[start + 1] -= inc. Only the single element at index start receives the increment.

5. Detailed Dry Run Walkthroughs

📋 Dry Run 1: length = 5, updates = [[1, 3, 2], [2, 4, 3], [0, 2, -2]]
Initial Difference Array (size 5): diff = [ 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 ] --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Step 1: Process Updates • Update 1: [1, 3, 2] (start = 1, end = 3, inc = 2) - diff[1] += 2 - end + 1 = 4 < 5 -> diff[4] -= 2 - diff = [ 0, 2, 0, 0, -2 ] • Update 2: [2, 4, 3] (start = 2, end = 4, inc = 3) - diff[2] += 3 - end + 1 = 5 (Out of bounds! No cancellation needed) - diff = [ 0, 2, 3, 0, -2 ] • Update 3: [0, 2, -2] (start = 0, end = 2, inc = -2) - diff[0] += -2 - end + 1 = 3 < 5 -> diff[3] -= (-2) => diff[3] += 2 - diff = [-2, 2, 3, 2, -2 ] --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Step 2: Prefix Sum Accumulation (In-Place) • i = 0: diff[0] = -2 • i = 1: diff[1] = diff[1] + diff[0] = 2 + (-2) = 0 • i = 2: diff[2] = diff[2] + diff[1] = 3 + 0 = 3 • i = 3: diff[3] = diff[3] + diff[2] = 2 + 3 = 5 • i = 4: diff[4] = diff[4] + diff[3] = -2 + 5 = 3 Final Result = [-2, 0, 3, 5, 3]
📋 Dry Run 2: Single-Element & Overlapping Ranges — length = 4, updates = [[1, 1, 5], [1, 3, 10], [0, 3, 1]]
Initial diff = [0, 0, 0, 0] • [1, 1, 5]: diff[1] += 5, diff[2] -= 5 -> [0, 5, -5, 0] • [1, 3, 10]: diff[1] += 10, end+1=4 (OOB) -> [0, 15, -5, 0] • [0, 3, 1]: diff[0] += 1, end+1=4 (OOB) -> [1, 15, -5, 0] Prefix Sum: • i = 0: 1 • i = 1: 15 + 1 = 16 • i = 2: -5 + 16 = 11 • i = 3: 0 + 11 = 11 Final Result = [1, 16, 11, 11]

6. Complexity Analysis Performance Metrics

Approach Category Time Complexity Space Complexity Operation Speed Performance Evaluation Rating
Approach 1: Naive Range Iteration O(K * N) O(1) Auxiliary 10^9 operations Sub-optimal / TLE. Mutates every index inside the range sequentially.
Approach 2: Difference Array (Optimal) O(N + K) O(1) Auxiliary 10^5 operations Absolute Production Standard. O(1) boundary updates per query followed by a single O(N) prefix sum pass.

Continuous Subarray Sum

Complete Technical & Mentorship Guide: Modular arithmetic invariants, prefix sum remainder hashing, minimum length-2 boundary handling, and detailed dry runs.

1. Problem Statement & Core Concept

Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if nums has a good subarray, or false otherwise.

A good subarray is a subarray where:

  • Its length is at least two (i.e. end - start + 1 >= 2), and
  • The sum of the elements of the subarray is a multiple of k (i.e. sum % k == 0).

Note: 0 is always a multiple of k (e.g. 0 * k = 0).

Continuous Subarray Sum Mechanics: Example 1: nums = [23, 2, 4, 6, 7], k = 6 - Subarray [2, 4] (indices 1 to 2): length = 2 >= 2 - Sum = 2 + 4 = 6 - 6 % 6 == 0 (Multiple of 6!) Output: true --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Example 2: nums = [23, 2, 6, 4, 7], k = 6 - Subarray [23, 2, 6, 4, 7] (indices 0 to 4): length = 5 >= 2 - Sum = 42 - 42 % 6 == 0 (Multiple of 6!) Output: true --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Example 3: nums = [23, 2, 6, 4, 7], k = 13 - No subarray of length >= 2 sums to a multiple of 13. Output: false

Constraints & Edge Traps

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
  • 0 <= sum(nums[i]) <= 2^31 - 1
  • 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1
  • Crucial Constraint: Length of the subarray MUST be at least 2. A single element divisible by k (e.g. nums = [6], k = 6) is INVALID!

2. Approach 1: Brute Force Subarray Sums (O(N^2) Time, O(1) Space)

🧭 Senior Mentor Explanation: The Brute Force Idea

Hey junior, the most direct approach to check for a good subarray is:

  1. Choose a starting index i from 0 to N - 2.
  2. Expand to ending index j from i + 1 to N - 1 (ensuring length is at least 2).
  3. Maintain a running sum curr_sum for the window nums[i..j].
  4. If curr_sum % k == 0, return true immediately!
Hinglish Explanation

Sabse basic tarika yeh hai ki hum 2 nested loops chalayein. Outer loop i se start kare aur inner loop j = i + 1 se aage badhe taaki length hamesha at least 2 rahe. Har step par running sum check karte jao: jaise hi sum % k == 0 mile, true return kar do. Lekin N = 10^5 ke liye N^2 = 10^10 operations honge, jisse TLE aayega.

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 1)

  1. n = len(nums): Get array size.
  2. for i in range(n - 1):: Start pointer i must leave at least one element for length >= 2.
  3. curr_sum = nums[i]: Initialize running sum with the first element.
  4. for j in range(i + 1, n):: Inner loop expands window from i + 1 onwards.
  5. curr_sum += nums[j]: Add current element to running sum.
  6. if curr_sum % k == 0: return True: If divisible, valid subarray found!
  7. return False: If no valid subarray is found after all combinations, return False.

Brute Force Implementation

class BruteForceSolution:
    def checkSubarraySum(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> bool:
        n = len(nums)
        # O(N^2) nested loop over all subarrays of length >= 2
        for i in range(n - 1):
            curr_sum = nums[i]
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                curr_sum += nums[j]
                if curr_sum % k == 0:
                    return True
        return False
class BruteForceSolution {
public:
    bool checkSubarraySum(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.size();
        for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; ++i) {
            long long currSum = nums[i];
            for (int j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {
                currSum += nums[j];
                if (currSum % k == 0) return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
};
class BruteForceSolution {
    public boolean checkSubarraySum(int[] nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.length;
        for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
            long currSum = nums[i];
            for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
                currSum += nums[j];
                if (currSum % k == 0) return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
}
var checkSubarraySumBF = function(nums, k) {
    const n = nums.length;
    for (let i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        let currSum = nums[i];
        for (let j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            currSum += nums[j];
            if (currSum % k === 0) return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
};

3. Approach 2: Optimal Prefix Sum Remainder Hashing (O(N) Time, O(min(N, K)) Space)

💡 Senior Mentor Explanation: The Modular Congruence Invariant

Junior, let's look at the mathematical relationship behind subarray sums and divisibility:

Let prefix[i] be the sum of elements from index 0 to i.

The sum of any subarray from index j + 1 to i is given by:

subarray_sum(j + 1 ... i) = prefix[i] - prefix[j]

We want this subarray sum to be a multiple of k:

(prefix[i] - prefix[j]) % k == 0 ==> prefix[i] % k == prefix[j] % k (Modular Congruence!)

The Golden Rule:

If the running prefix sum modulo k produces a remainder rem that we have ALREADY SEEN at an earlier index j, then the subarray between j + 1 and i MUST have a sum that is a multiple of k!

How to handle length >= 2:

  • We store the EARLIEST index where each remainder was seen in a Hash Map: remainder_map = { remainder : earliest_index }.
  • When remainder rem appears again at index i, check distance: i - remainder_map[rem] >= 2.
  • If distance >= 2, return true!
  • If distance < 2, do NOT update the index! (Keeping the earliest index gives us the widest possible window for future checks).

Why initialize remainder_map = {0: -1}?

If a prefix starting from index 0 itself is divisible by k (e.g. nums = [23, 1], k = 6 where sum at index 1 is 24 and 24 % 6 == 0), the distance from the imaginary baseline index -1 is 1 - (-1) = 2 >= 2, which correctly confirms a valid subarray of length 2!

Hinglish Explanation

Mathematics ka rule hai: agar do alag prefix sums ka % k remainder SAME aata hai, toh unke beech ke elements ka sum k se exactly divide hoga! Hum ek Hash Map me { remainder: first_seen_index } store karte hain. Jab bhi purana remainder wapas mile aur current index ka gap >= 2 ho, hum turant true return kar dete hain. {0: -1} daalna zaroori hai taaki index 0 se shuru hone wale valid subarrays handle ho sakein.

Remainder Hash Map Trace: nums = [23, 2, 4, 6, 7], k = 6 Initial: remainder_map = { 0: -1 } Running Sum = 0 • i = 0 (num = 23): - sum = 0 + 23 = 23 - rem = 23 % 6 = 5 - rem 5 not in map -> store { 5: 0 } - Map: { 0: -1, 5: 0 } • i = 1 (num = 2): - sum = 23 + 2 = 25 - rem = 25 % 6 = 1 - rem 1 not in map -> store { 1: 1 } - Map: { 0: -1, 5: 0, 1: 1 } • i = 2 (num = 4): - sum = 25 + 4 = 29 - rem = 29 % 6 = 5 - rem 5 is ALREADY IN MAP! Earliest index was 0. - Check length: i - map[5] = 2 - 0 = 2 >= 2 (Valid Good Subarray!) - Subarray is nums[1..2] = [2, 4] with sum 6 (% 6 == 0). Output: True!

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 2)

  1. rem_map = {0: -1}: Seed the map with remainder 0 at index -1 to handle valid subarrays starting at index 0.
  2. running_sum = 0: Running accumulator for array elements.
  3. for i, num in enumerate(nums):: Loop through each index i and value num.
  4. running_sum += num: Add current number to prefix sum.
  5. rem = running_sum % k: Calculate modulo remainder.
  6. if rem in rem_map:: Check if this remainder was seen before.
    • if i - rem_map[rem] >= 2: return True: If the distance between current index and earliest occurrence is at least 2, return True!
  7. else: rem_map[rem] = i: If remainder is seen for the first time, record its index. (Never overwrite an existing remainder!).
  8. return False: Return False if no valid subarray is found after full traversal.

Optimal Hash Map Implementation

class Solution:
    def checkSubarraySum(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> bool:
        # Map stores: { remainder : earliest_index_seen }
        rem_map = {0: -1}
        running_sum = 0

        for i, num in enumerate(nums):
            running_sum += num
            rem = running_sum % k

            # HIGHLIGHT: Check if same remainder was seen at least 2 indices ago
            if rem in rem_map:
                if i - rem_map[rem] >= 2:
                    return True
            else:
                # Store only the EARLIEST index to maximize subarray length
                rem_map[rem] = i

        return False
class Solution {
public:
    bool checkSubarraySum(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
        unordered_map<int, int> remMap;
        remMap[0] = -1; // Base case for sub-arrays starting at index 0

        long long runningSum = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); ++i) {
            runningSum += nums[i];
            int rem = runningSum % k;

            if (remMap.count(rem)) {
                if (i - remMap[rem] >= 2) {
                    return true;
                }
            } else {
                remMap[rem] = i;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }
};
class Solution {
    public boolean checkSubarraySum(int[] nums, int k) {
        Map<Integer, Integer> remMap = new HashMap<>();
        remMap.put(0, -1);

        int runningSum = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
            runningSum += nums[i];
            int rem = runningSum % k;

            if (remMap.containsKey(rem)) {
                if (i - remMap.get(rem) >= 2) {
                    return true;
                }
            } else {
                remMap.put(rem, i);
            }
        }

        return false;
    }
}

    remMap.set(0, -1);

            if (i - remMap.get(rem) >= 2) {
                return true;
            }
        } else {
            remMap.set(rem, i);
        }
    }

    return false;
};

4. Boundary Traps & Edge Case Analysis

⚠️ Common Traps & Edge Cases

1. Consecutive Zeros (e.g. nums = [0, 0], k = 1):
sum = 0 + 0 = 0. 0 % 1 == 0 with length 2. rem_map = {0: -1} -> at i = 1, rem = 0, distance 1 - (-1) = 2 >= 2 -> returns True correctly!

2. Overwriting Hash Map Indices (The Greedy Trap):
If rem is already present in the map, NEVER overwrite its index! We want to keep the earliest index so that future duplicate remainders have the largest possible distance (i - earliest_index).

3. Single Element Divisible by k (e.g. nums = [6], k = 6):
At i = 0, rem = 0. Distance 0 - (-1) = 1 < 2. Loop ends and returns False, correctly enforcing length >= 2.

5. Detailed Dry Run Walkthroughs

(First seen at index 0) - Distance check: i - rem_map[5] = 2 - 0 = 2 >= 2 (Valid!) Returns True immediately!
📋 Dry Run 2: Subarray Starting at Index 0 — nums = [23, 1, 6], k = 6
Initial State: rem_map = { 0: -1 } • i = 0 (num = 23): - running_sum = 23 -> rem = 5 - rem_map = { 0: -1, 5: 0 } • i = 1 (num = 1): - running_sum = 24 -> rem = 0 - rem 0 IS in rem_map! (First seen at index -1) - Distance check: 1 - (-1) = 2 >= 2 (Valid!) Returns True immediately!
📋 Dry Run 3: Single Zero Divisible Trap — nums = [5, 0, 0], k = 3
Initial State: rem_map = { 0: -1 } • i = 0 (num = 5): - running_sum = 5 -> rem = 2 - rem_map = { 0: -1, 2: 0 } • i = 1 (num = 0): - running_sum = 5 -> rem = 2 - rem 2 is in rem_map! - Distance: 1 - 0 = 1 < 2 (Invalid! Only 1 element [0]). - Do NOT overwrite rem_map[2]! Keep rem_map[2] = 0. • i = 2 (num = 0): - running_sum = 5 -> rem = 2 - rem 2 is in rem_map! - Distance: 2 - 0 = 2 >= 2 (Valid! Subarray [0, 0] of length 2). Returns True!

LeetCode 992 Hard Master Edition

Subarrays with K Different Integers

Complete Technical & Mentorship Guide: Why standard sliding windows fail for exact counts, the reduction to AtMost(K) - AtMost(K - 1), single-pass 3-pointer optimizations, and detailed dry runs.

1. Problem Statement & Core Concept

Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of good subarrays of nums.

A good array is an array where the number of different integers in that array is exactly k.

A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.

Subarrays with K Distinct Integers Visualization: Example 1: nums = [1, 2, 1, 2, 3], k = 2 Subarrays with EXACTLY 2 distinct integers: 1. nums[0..1] = [1, 2] -> {1, 2} (2 distinct) 2. nums[0..2] = [1, 2, 1] -> {1, 2} (2 distinct) 3. nums[0..3] = [1, 2, 1, 2] -> {1, 2} (2 distinct) 4. nums[1..2] = [2, 1] -> {1, 2} (2 distinct) 5. nums[1..3] = [2, 1, 2] -> {1, 2} (2 distinct) 6. nums[2..3] = [1, 2] -> {1, 2} (2 distinct) 7. nums[3..4] = [2, 3] -> {2, 3} (2 distinct) Total Count: 7 Output: 7 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Example 2: nums = [1, 2, 1, 3, 4], k = 3 Subarrays with EXACTLY 3 distinct integers: 1. nums[0..3] = [1, 2, 1, 3] -> {1, 2, 3} 2. nums[1..3] = [2, 1, 3] -> {1, 2, 3} 3. nums[2..4] = [1, 3, 4] -> {1, 3, 4} Total Count: 3 Output: 3

Constraints

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^4
  • 1 <= nums[i], k <= nums.length

2. Approach 1: Brute Force Counting (O(N^2) Time, O(U) Space)

🧭 Senior Mentor Explanation: The Brute Force Idea

Hey junior, the most direct approach to count subarrays with k distinct elements is:

  1. Fix a starting index i from 0 to n - 1.
  2. Expand an ending index j from i to n - 1.
  3. Maintain a hash set or frequency map of elements seen in nums[i..j].
  4. If the number of unique elements is equal to k, increment our total count: ans += 1.
  5. If unique elements exceed k, expanding j further will only add more unique numbers (or keep it > k); we can break early for this i.
Hinglish Explanation

Sabse basic tarika yeh hai ki hum har possible subarray nums[i..j] generate karein. Ek hash set se unique elements count karein. Jab set ka size k ho jaye, tab answer badha do. Agar set ka size k se bada ho jaye, toh aage check karne ka koi fayda nahi kyonki unique numbers aur badhenge hi. Lekin N = 2 * 10^4 ke liye N^2 = 4 * 10^8 operations honge, jisse TLE aayega.

Line-by-Line Code Breakdown (Approach 1)

  1. n = len(nums), ans = 0: Initialize array size and answer counter.
  2. for i in range(n):: Outer loop chooses the starting boundary i.
  3. distinct = set(): Initialize set to track unique elements in current subarray.
  4. for j in range(i, n):: Inner loop expands right boundary j.
  5. distinct.add(nums[j]): Add current number to the distinct tracker.
  6. if len(distinct) == k: ans += 1: If exactly k distinct integers exist, record valid subarray.
  7. elif len(distinct) > k: break: If unique count exceeds k, further expansion is invalid; break inner loop.
  8. return ans: Return total count of matching subarrays.

Brute Force Implementation

class BruteForceSolution:
    def subarraysWithKDistinct(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        ans = 0
        
        for i in range(n):
            distinct = set()
            for j in range(i, n):
                distinct.add(nums[j])
                if len(distinct) == k:
                    ans += 1
                elif len(distinct) > k:
                    break
                    
        return ans
class BruteForceSolution {
public:
    int subarraysWithKDistinct(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.size();
        int ans = 0;
        
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            unordered_set<int> distinct;
            for (int j = i; j < n; ++j) {
                distinct.insert(nums[j]);
                if (distinct.size() == k) {
                    ans++;
                } else if (distinct.size() > k) {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        return ans;
    }
};
class BruteForceSolution {
    public int subarraysWithKDistinct(int[] nums, int k) {
        int n = nums.length;
        int ans = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            Set<Integer> distinct = new HashSet<>();
            for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
                distinct.add(nums[j]);
                if (distinct.size() == k) {
                    ans++;
                } else if (distinct.size() > k) {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        return ans;
    }
}
